geeklist.title: BGG.CON Virtual Flea Market 2025
geeklist.description:
[center][COLOR=#009933][size=18][b] Welcome to this year's BGG.CON Virtual Flea Market 2025! STARTED OCTOBER 1, 2025[/b][/size][/COLOR][/center] [poll=2127959] c[enter][size=14][b]BGG.CON 2025 VFM Table Assignments!! Final Version 23![/b][/size][ImageID=9217969 large][/center]
[center][size=14][b]PARTICIPANTS MUST READ THE ENTIRE DESCRIPTION!![/b][/size][/center]Since this Geeklist will get very long, the Rules of the BGG.CON Virtual Flea Market 2024 are listed under the first three games on the first page. Participants are required to read and understand all the requirements: :arrowE: [listitem=12102315]Participation Requirements[/listitem] :arrowE: [listitem=12102317]Buyers Requirements[/listitem] :arrowE: [listitem=12102319]Sellers Requirements[/listitem] [center][size=18]Virtual Flea Market Introduction![/size][/center]For people who are traveling to the convention, sellers only want to bring games that they have sold. Buyers want to plan how much space they need to bring games home. Enter the Virtual Flea Market. If you have items that you'd like to sell at BGG.Con, list them here with the condition of your items, the price, and terms (Auction, Buy it now, whatever) you'd like to sell for with only a 3% commission. Buyers settle on a price with the seller. At the con, [u]buyers give an envelope with pre-counted money to the seller[/u] who hands them the game! Quick, easy, and 4000 games exchange hands in one hour! [u]Note that the Virtual Flea Market is different from the Math Trade and different from the BGG.CON Bazaar![/u]
This is a VERY big event, with about 11,000 games, 200 sellers, and 500 buyers. We require everyone to be [u]respectful and to follow through with their commitments.[/u] In past years this event has threatened to get out of control which would cancel this event for everyone. [b]This year I will be far less tolerant of anyone not following the rules.[/b] If you do not follow the rules, I will just delete your items. Geeklist item number is NOT guaranteed. If you want to bookmark an item, click on the DATE of the item, and bookmark [u]that[/u] on your quickbar. That is a permanent link.
[b]Summary Links:[/b] Need to request a game? Check out: [geeklist=363944][/geeklist] Want to search the VFM for BGG.Con 2025 GeekList? (These are still being set up for this year.) 👉 [url=https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/363504]Eric Bettan's alphabetical search tool hereEric Bettan's alphabetical search tool here[/url] 👉 [url=https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l= 363504&mode=9&sort=0]David Rathbun's Updated search tool here[/url]
Remember: Read The THREE listed games for the full participation requirements: :arrowE: [listitem=12102315]Participation Requirements[/listitem] :arrowE: [listitem=12102317]Buyers Requirements[/listitem] :arrowE: [listitem=12102319]Sellers Requirements[/listitem] .

Hi all! A lot of you will remember me as the one that was on a mission to supply every submarine in the U.S. Navy with a compact board game library. Each of which has been memorialized with the name(s) of a fallen hero or more throughout American history. This year my missions: continued financial assistance to Gold Star families in Arizona; support packages to ALL American deployed soldiers worldwide and financial assistance for our grandson (honor student since middle school-now in 11th grade and taking engineering college classes) who has been invited to join a national honor benefit program. This program invites only honor students on an educational tour of Asia IF they earn the money on their own to go. He needs to earn $5,000 (he has worked very hard: many family members have pledged $ for every “A” he earns on his report cards; every free weekend he has poop scooped, painted, washed cars, sold chocolate chip cookies he baked, cleaned garages/attics, handy-man work for the elderly in our community, yard work and more & has $1,100 left to earn to complete his trip earnings). The proceeds from my game sales this year will go to these missions and to our grandson as hourly wages when he performs continued work in our community! THANK YOU TO ALL OF YOU for helping me achieve the goal for the currently commissioned submarines and supporting my other missions! I am currently assembling an undisclosed number of libraries which, upon request, will be provided to the Navy for “potential future subs”. I have uploaded a few photos below so you can see how you helped!! (*I hope to post many games this weekend). [b]Recommendation to buyers:[/b] Keep track of your bids and purchases in a separate spreadsheet or notepad. Include the game name, price, real name and handle of the seller, and most importantly, a direct link to the item listing. A lot of sellers are putting "sold" in their listing without linking the buyer and/or not marking the item sold. Both of which make it difficult to go back and find the stuff you've won or bid on.
[b]Plea to sellers:[/b] Please update your listings to include the word "sold" and a user link to the buyer AND mark the item sold. This will ensure that items can be easily tracked by your buyers and minimize confusion later.

Deleting items shouldn't matter. Numbers can change; it's not a good way to track Geeklist items. BGG provides a very easy way to track things you care about - the subscribe button. (Edit: For Geeklist items the Subscribe option is part of the "kebab" button - the three dots.) You can then go to Subscriptions (dropdown from your avatar button in the top menu) > Subscriptions > Geeklist Items. And you will see all Geeklist Items you've subscribed to.
Alternatively, you can keep a list of links directly to those items somewhere, e.g. a Google Sheet. Those links do not break if other items get deleted or added.
Alternatively, if you have commented on an item, you can go to a list of all Geeklist Items you've commented on, in the format "https://boardgamegeek.com/comments/listitem/<your username here>"
That said, I haven't deleted items because I know people get upset about it, but it happens every year and I'm not sure why then people don't adjust....

I think the real deal here is: if we want something to work a particular way, we have to make/use a system that only allows it to work that way. This system is so flexible that some people are just bound to miss some rules or skirt some. It's okay. It's not the end of the world. It's annoying and unfortunate, but it's just how things are. If we want this to be different, the much more effective way to address it is to ask BGG to actually make a system that works with deletions or allows you to turn off deletions or takes meta data better so it automatically handles it. They make improvements every year and they could definitely add all these features!

...but it does work with deletions. It's much more reasonable to track items using one of the various methods provided and supported by the site (that I described above) than to hope they will change the site to support some other method(s) people want to use for whatever reasons.

[q="BiscuityGoodness"]I think I may have been doing this wrong? Was I supposed to do all of my many, many offers on other people's items as a "bundle offer via PM" while also saying that the prices on my items listed for sale are "non-negotiable"? 🙃[/q]
This is the problem with listing your items as a i'll do a bulk discount if you buy multiple items. people immediately take to dms to buy a bunch of items at a discount. When items are fresh and there is competition it's easy for this to become a mess of figuring out which bundles work with which offers full prices.
If i wanted 10 games from a person and offered say 30% off and wrote that well then if person y wants just 1 of those games they may jump in to try and bin it. Which is totally fine but the owner may still be incentivized to take my discounted offer to move the other 9 games that don't have an offer on them. If i listed my discount 10 games prices people might try and offer 1-3 dollars more to still get a discount and break up the bundle. At least by saying bin sending an offer it says i'm wanting to buy it if you want to take my bulk price. Nothing is stopping others from also putting an offer of what they want to pay if the deal falls through but at least people know someone sent interest. People used to just send offers via dm and then someone else would bid/bin and the item thinking they were the only offer then watch the item get sold to someone else due to a pm deal and that feels bad because you had no idea there was other interest.
I prefer open negotiation on bundles. This isn't Diplomacy.

[q="Tolio"]People used to just send offers via dm and then someone else would bid/bin and the item thinking they were the only offer then watch the item get sold to someone else due to a pm deal and that feels bad because you had no idea there was other interest.[/q]
This is part of why I just offer a public discount if you spend enough with me. Want 25% off? Make your own bundle and BIN all the stuff you want publicly at the discount price. Just a lot simpler and cleaner than haggling over a mystery value that we might or might not agree upon.

Yes, all is true. Whether you need/want access during VFM setup time comes down to your personal situation. People like Steph Hodge selling 80+ games need time to setup that many games at a table.
For me, I always fly to BGG and I am never going to fly with more games than can fit in my carry-on and a checked bag. I also prefer to finalize as many sales and purchases as possible outside of the VFM hour between my games or even between my turns during heavy games. That means that I usually only need to take a small stack of games with me to the VFM room and walk away with a small stack as well. That also means that I do not need to enlist a helper and I do not need to deal with the elevator traffic jam before/after the VFM hour.
I understand why people want to just finalize all their transactions during the actual VFM. My preference is to minimize the amount of time I have to deal with the congestion/chaos of that two-hour block; when you account for time hauling your sales to the VFM and dropping purchases off in your room.

Where some confusion can come it is that a game can register as sold, but not as bought.
For example, I bought [url=https://bgg.cc/geeklist/363504/bggcon-virtual-flea-market-2025?itemid=12205115#12205115]America[/url]. It shows up in the[url=https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/363504?Seller=jtt005&Status=Sold&Sort=Name] seller's sold stats[/url], but not in my [url=https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/363504?Buyer=parliboy&Status=Sold&Sort=Name]bought stats[/url]. This sort of thing is going to happen when the seller doesn't complete all the suggested steps.
So like Solomar said, check the sold stats only if you want reliable data.

Also since deleting is verboten you end up with fake "sales" when people just put "sold" in the description to take a listing off the market, so to speak. I don't think that really skews the table assignments too much, though.

What does FP stand for?
[q="SavageSpawn"]What does FP stand for?[/q] Usually firm price.
[q="lancefriday945"][q="SavageSpawn"]What does FP stand for?[/q] Usually firm price.[/q] I use it for "Fixed Price" as opposed to an auction.

[q="SavageSpawn"]What does FP stand for?[/q] FP = Fixed Price (not an auction although some sellers will consider offers) SB = Starting Bid (Auction = the minimum price a seller is willing to sell the item for) BIN = Buy it Now (Auction = a "skip the auction and just buy it" price that the seller may or may not provide)

While I generally agree with the prior comments, I want to add my written thoughts on the survey.
[q]1. Do we need to stick to strictly alphabetical by username?[/q]
No. At this point most of us know where to go. For the people who don't, they can ask. The table assignments are how I sort my envelopes. That said, when you publish the final map, please continue to list by name order instead of table order.
[q]2.What do we do with sellers of a large number of games which fill a table to overflowing?[/q]
I didn't vote with the plurality here, but maybe my rationale is wrong. My thought is to get it so more games are at the front of the room and so people who are only buying one or two things are in and out faster. Other people might feel that the prolific sellers can create clogs in the movement in the room and so want them in the back.
[q]3.Do we need custom signs every year?[/q]
Many of your prolific sellers already have their own signs, so your signs don't really do anything for them. The rest of us can figure it out. But if you want to split the baby, just give us blank tents at the door and let us fill in our usernames ourselves on the tents. It's a lot simpler and it's only going to take thirty seconds for us to do. And it alleviates for you the stress of having to do it all last minute.
I also bet on the front vs back, several folks lots of folks don't care between the 2 (I know I dont)...back gets them out of the way but front is easier for them to haul in.

If you're selling or buying, then you should be following the VFM list the entire time. If you're selling, you should be able to look at the assignment chart and see where you are located. If you're a buyer, you should be following the recommendations to have cash in envelopes and write the location on it, or if paying electronically just jot down what tables you are picking up at. I'm for reducing the work for the organizer.

[q="Woolvey"]I'm all for reducing workloads. I think most of us can read a grid and lookup where we need to go. If someone can't, they must be the Chameleon! 🙂
Q2 seems to imply that single seller tables are going to be busier and should be treated differently. Presumably, when the other sellers are being combined to share tables, the result is combined tables with a total number of games not that much different to the single-table sellers, but with arguably more people behind them. I see no reason to try to keep single-seller tables together at the front or back, and think it may be better to intermingle them with the shared tables. However, Q2 is the least important to me and I'd be happy with whatever is easiest to organize.[/q]
Basically, taking the sellers with 100-150 items to the back wall gives them more room to interact with buyers, and keeps traffic flowing in the middle of the room. It also allows them to have boxes and personal carts by the back wall out of the way. They still would be alphabetical (A10-H10), but pulled out of the rest of the alphabetized tables. So if Jan is selling 100 items, and Joe has a single table for 10, and Jumpy has 150, then Jan and Jumpy get tables in the back. This allows me to combine Jabby (10), Joe (10), and Julie (10) on one table. It also makes it so that no table has 4 or 5 sellers anymore. I only have to do that because of the forced large tables in the alphabet. I could get it down to a max of 3 people at a table because the larger tables are moved to the back.
[q="parliboy"]That said, when you publish the final map, please continue to list by name order instead of table order.[/q] Yes, it would stay the same. The large sellers would be highlighted as being in the back.
[q="parliboy"]I didn't vote with the plurality here, but maybe my rationale is wrong. My thought is to get it so more games are at the front of the room and so people who are only buying one or two things are in and out faster. Other people might feel that the prolific sellers can create clogs in the movement in the room and so want them in the back..[/q] I get what you are saying, but I was thinking of the large sellers being able to use the back wall for boxes and their own personal carts.
[q="parliboy"]Many of your prolific sellers already have their own signs, so your signs don't really do anything for them. The rest of us can figure it out. But if you want to split the baby, just give us blank tents at the door and let us fill in our usernames ourselves on the tents. It's a lot simpler and it's only going to take thirty seconds for us to do. And it alleviates for you the stress of having to do it all last minute.[/q]Hey, good idea!

So as a person who has been doing this since the dark days of the room which felt like being a stock market bro on the exchange floor and as a coordinator here is my take.
1) as long as it's roughly alphabetical combine away i wouldn't go putting L's in row 1 but not being strictly alphabetical is what i do and haven't seen a ton of issue. Where i got confused people is when i did some of that due to people wanting to share tables, even with picture and table signs having an o on A5 still had people asking me/tg where they were at.
2) Honestly the rooms get a ton of people everywhere and the front and back have people stop to fill bags/rebalance store stuff etc. So if suddenly large sellers are there I'd say i haven't really seen any one seller no matter the size be a big issue so far no matter where they are. Except the person who has 50+ games to sell and shows up 30 min late which causes a storm to descend on that one spot
3) The signs are super helpful i feel and i still see a lot of confused people lost on who is who at these things. Could it be reduced to just the table numbers? probably, but i do think it's worth the names still. Maybe instead of doing all the folding to make them table stands we just do some tape and a full sheet like the Bazaar does and tape them to the front of the tables. To me i spend 30 min making the table signs and like 3 hours folding the stupid things putting them on a full sheet seems so much simpler. Yes people would make their own signs if they go away but i'd wager that only be a small % of the group as even during the dark days only about half the room had signs. And being a person at the last row of tables i'm frequently waiting till 5 min after the vfm ends for my last pickup because it took someone over an hour to walk and find their sellers as they started in A. i'd prefer to keep things that encourage it to go faster and removing names does not aid that ideal.

I totally agree with the do what makes your life easier sentiment, and the we are fully capable of making our own signs. As far as room flow I agree that having all the people selling massive amounts of games along one side would help those that are only selling/buying a few things have an easier time of it. And Thank you @Solamar for organizing this. It is greatly appreciated.

[center][COLOR=#009933][size=18][b]1. Participation Requirements[/b][/size][/COLOR][/center] [u][b]1.1 Expectations[/b][/u] Since this event has gotten so large (also fun and successful), we need everyone's help to keep the event organized so we can continue it in future years. Please be [b]polite and courteous[/b] in all your communication. Be patient and help others. Be on time. There is nothing more frustrating than walking through the room looking for someone, only to find out they are running late or wandering about the hall.
[u][b]1.2 Date & Location: [/b][/u] Held in Reunion EFGH Thursday evening (6p-7p VFM Seller Setup, 7p-8p VFM). * Please send your [b]thanks to Jeff Anderson[/b] and the BGG.CON team for continuing to allow us to have the VFM for BGG.CON! * I (Sterling Babcock, [user=Solamar]Solamar[/user]) will be running the Virtual Flea Market and attending. My wife, Marcia (RedPhoenixNia) will also be helping me as well as Team Geek members. * We won't be requiring masks but [u]we do recommend masks in this crowded situation[/u]. Please remember the general Health & Safety Guidelines: "Respect the personal choices of those around you. This includes the choice to wear or not wear a mask."
[u][b]1.3 Room Plan[/b][/u] Posted the final week before BGG.CON on the main header. In general (almost) all sellers will have space at a table if they sell roughly 5 games or more.
[u][b]1.4 Not following through with commitments[/b][/u] Unfortunately, in recent years there are too many sellers/buyers backing out of deals, and it is taking an inordinate amount of time. The VFM is just so big that I cannot be an intermediary to get buyers and sellers to communicate and resolve issues. [b]Sellers must have their games to sell before they list them. Buyers must follow through with commitments which they made months ago even if a lower price is posted. If something unexpected comes up both need to come to some sort of mutual agreement and may require compensation for lost opportunity to sell.[/b] Both sides should also notify me of the resolution. If this is not done, I will unfortunately have to ban users from participation in the virtual flea market. If you are contacted by me in geekmail, [u]you need to respond immediately[/u] and work things out with the other party to mutual agreement. Buyers who fail to make their committed purchase will be reported to Matthew Monin (Octavian). (This is a very small minority, so if you have not already been contacted by me, then it is not you.)
[u][b]1.5 Shipping Games[/u][/b]: See the BGG.CON Master list for FedEx delivery information.
[u][b]1.6 Tuesday Night Meetup[/b][/u] Since BGG.CON does not officially take any hotel space on Tuesday, there can be no official or unofficial events prior to Wednesday.
+sold+

[center][COLOR=#009933][size=18][b]2. Buyers Requirements[/b][/size][/COLOR][/center] [u][b]2.1 Buyers Room Plan[/b][/u] Sellers tables will continue to be [b]listed by BGG username[/b] in [u]approximate[/u] alphabetical order. [u]Sellers may be rearranged a bit out of order[/u] to facilitate dividing up the tables by number of games sold. There will be an alphabetical list of sellers at the door which will indicate the exact row and column of a particular sellers table (e.g. G5). [b]You can look up who you are purchasing from ahead of time, and mark them on your purchase envelopes AHEAD OF TIME[/b]. That will help you find the seller quickly and efficiently. Signs on tables will make it easier to find them.
[u][b]2.2 Buyer Guidelines[/b][/u] 2.2.1 [b]All buyers MUST be BGG.CON attendees to participate in the virtual flea market[/b]. Team Geek will be at the doors to enforce this, and buyers should not purchase from sellers who are not attending BGG.CON.
2.2.2 Commitments: [b]Buyers and Sellers must follow through with commitments[/b]. See Rule 1.5!
2.2.3 [b]Verify before you buy![/b] If you are expecting that special promo to be in a package of games, ASK for a photograph from the seller to PROVE they have exactly what you want before you commit to buy.
2.2.4 Summary of Unsold Games and Request Geeklist - Use one of these links for an alphabetized list of games still available[/u] :arrowE: Alphabetical search tool courtesy of Eric Bettan (Carnage994): https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/363504 :arrowE: Here’s another search list function by David Rathbun: https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l=363504 :arrowE: If there is something you are looking for, think about adding it to the BGG.Con Virtual Flea Market Request List. [geeklist=TBD][/geeklist]
2.2.5 Buyers MUST attend the START of the 7 pm hour of exchange and stay until all your games are received. Do NOT be late and make sellers wait for you! Buyers are REQUIRED to either show up, or notify the Seller they will not be there. Do NOT be 'that guy' which makes a seller wait all hour trying to find you. You must find the seller! Buyers stay on the OUTSIDE of the tables for ease of finding games. Buyers may not use hotel luggage carts.
2.2.6 If you are a [b]buyer[/b], bring one envelope for each seller you are buying from. [b]Each envelope should be marked on the outside with the seller's user name, table assignment, and the items you are buying and should contain exact change![/b] After doing this for a few years, we can tell you that this makes the event go much more smoothly for everyone. Put your name on your envelopes so it's easily identified as paid by sellers or in case it gets lost.
2.2.7: Create a spreadsheet with the games you're buying. Create columns for Game Name, Game Cost, Method of Payment, Seller Name, Seller BGG Username, Comments, etc. If you're paying via PayPal, Venmo, etc. make a note. Print off your list prior to the event and bring it with you. Bring bags to haul off your 'new' games. You won't be able to use the luggage carts.
2.2.8 Any attempt by a buyer to deceive the seller and pick up a game which you did not rightfully purchase will be dealt with harshly.
2.2.9 [b][u]BGG.CON Bazaar Marketplace[/b][/u] The BGG.CON Bazaar Marketplace is a separate event run at 10 am on Friday, where you can explore and purchase games at the con. It is not related to the Virtual Flea Market, but please do attend!
+sold+

[center][COLOR=#009933][size=18][b]3. Sellers Requirements[/b][/size][/COLOR][/center] [u][b]3.1 Sellers Room Plan[/b][/u] In general all sellers will have space at a table if you sell roughly 5 games or more. If less than that, you may need to meet individually. I will entertain sellers combining if needed, but you will need to notify me AND tell the buyers to go to that persons username table. [u]Sellers may be rearranged a bit out of order[/u] to facilitate dividing up the tables by number of games sold. There will be an alphabetical list of sellers at the door which will indicate the exact row and column of a particular sellers table. There are 80 tables. There will be no ticket to sign up for sellers tables. I will assign a table to each seller up to our capacity. If you do not get a table because you sold too few games, you are on your own to arrange the exchange with the buyer.
[u][b]3.2 Seller Guidelines[/b][/u] 3.2.1 [b]All sellers MUST be BGG.CON attendees to participate in the virtual flea market[/b]. Team Geek will be at the doors to enforce this, and sellers should not sell to buyers who are not attending BGG.CON.
3.2.2 Commitments: [b]Buyers and Sellers must follow through with commitments[/b]. See Rule 1.5!
3.2.3 Sellers must have their games to sell before they list them.
3.2.4 Please do add your items to this list! You choose how to sell your items: Fixed Price, Auction, Dutch Auction. You should monitor your own items.
3.2.5 [b][u]Do NOT delete your item[/u].[/b] People expect items to remain historically. If you must remove an item, Mark them as sold or no longer available, but do not delete the item.
3.2.6 [u][b]Any Auctions must have a stated end date and conclude by November 1.[/b][/u] Games must be marked sold by November 2 so that we know to assign you a table. I cannot monitor and contact sellers about 11,000 items. If I see an auction without an end date by November 1, I will simply delete your item from the list. (This deadline does not apply to BIN since you will mark the game sold when it is sold in order to get table space.)
3.2.7 [u][b]Math Trade[/b][/u] If you participate in the BGG.Con Math Trade, make sure that items are NOT listed in both at the same time. This will not be monitored. If you do so, it is [u]your[/u] responsibility to immediately mark items sold as no longer available in the Math trade, and mark them deleted from this list if they are traded. If you make a mistake and sell a game twice, it is your responsibility to fulfill all your commitments, [u]no matter what the cost is to you[/u]. It is far better that you avoid conflicts like this.
3.2.8 Sellers should arrange a bulk commission at the BGG Marketplace or individually by game.
3.2.9 Any attempt by a seller to deceive a buyer by significantly miss describing the item (e.g. missing specified expansion) will be dealt with harshly.
3.2.10 Sellers will be allowed into the room to set up between 6-6:45pm on Thursday evening. No games will be allowed into the room after 6:45 pm. Sellers stay on INSIDE of tables. Do NOT block the outside traffic with games! You are expected to [u]be at your sellers table on time for the full hour[/u] or until all your games are sold. If you cannot attend the VFM due to unforeseen circumstances, notify me and make that clear to your buyers in your listing. Sellers may not use hotel luggage carts. If you are also a buyer, you must make other time arrangements to do your VFW pickups outside the VFW event, or have another person do your pickups during the VFW. You must remain at your sellers table.
3.2.11 Make sure you take the $$$ out of the Envelopes and throw the envelopes in the trash. Don't leave them for me to clean up!
3.2.12 List Aggregator Tools: - If your item is an auction, please include the word "[b]Auction[/b]" someplace. (It helps the aggregator tools) - If you are selling an item that deserves an [b]alternate name[/b] in a summary list (i.e. Misc Game Accessory), please place this code in your item someplace: "+altname+ Detailed Title -altname-" - [u]Mark sold items as: [b]SOLD[/b] so that the summary tools[/u] can remove it from the available list using +sold+. Mark who purchased it as well. - If you change your price, [u]please keep the new price on the same line of the geeklist[/u] (Do something like [-]$25[/-] $20)
3.2.13 There is an [u]easy way to add items[/u] to the geeklist, courtesy of Eric Bettan (Carnage994): Alphabetical search tool: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/363504 The link to add games is: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/363504
3.2.14: At the end if you decide to share tables with someone, please geekmail me, and please make it CLEAR: "X is at table Y", not "Y and X are sharing tables but I am not telling you which."
[u][b]Tips from Past Sellers[/b][/u]: 1. Create a spreadsheet with the games you're selling. Create columns for Game Name, Game Cost, Method of Payment, Buyer Name, Buyer BGG Name, Buyer Table Assignment, Comments, etc. If you’re paying via PayPal, Venmo, etc. make a note. Print off your list prior to the event and bring it with you. Print out the table assignments beforehand. Circle your table. I recommend using mail merge from the spreadsheet to create Removable Sticky notes on the game with the name of the Buyer picking up your games.
2. Send out geek mails and confirm with the game sale with people who have bought games from you. Sometimes people miss responses on the geeklist.
[u][b]Adding Games to the List[/b][/u] The easy way to add items to the VFM geeklist: 1. Add all your items to [u]your[/u] BGG games collection list. 2. Tag items [b]for trade[/b] in your BGG collection. Note: This won't include expansions at this time. 3. Then use [geekurl=/geekgold/transfer/user/Carnage994]Eric Bettan[/geekurl]'s (feel free to tip him) posting tool with instructions to add games: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/363504 4. Type in your BGG [b]Username[/b] and click [b]load[/b]. 5. Your list will be populated. 6. Simply add notes to the field that says [b]"Message to add on each entry"[/b] for example: [size=9] Additional Notes: 1. Let's meet up at the VFM Thursday from 7pm to 8pm. 2. I accept Cash (exact change in an envelope), Paypal, Zelle, or Venmo. 3. I am open to discounts on multiple game buys. Please post here and/or send a Geekmail with any questions." [/size] 7. In the "Buy it now" field enter the price of the game. 8. Then Click "[b]Add Item[/b]". 9. Rinse, wash, and repeat.
[b]Use Item Tags[/b] in your listing: +altname+ Whatever You'd Like To Title Your Item -altname- The +sold+ tag avoids improperly tagging an item as sold simply because the word "sold" appears in the listing, perhaps in the game name or something. The tag +remove+ is used to remove an item from the list aggregator tools without actually deleting it from the Geek List.
+sold+
item.comment:
To preface my question, I always fly to BGG and I never fly with enough sales cargo to really warrant being assigned VFM table space; so I do not care about being assigned table space.
Regarding 3.2.6, is there a is there a similar deadline respective to fixed-price listings?

[q="das_ninja"]To preface my question, I always fly to BGG and I never fly with enough sales cargo to really warrant being assigned VFM table space; so I do not care about being assigned table space. Regarding 3.2.6, is there a is there a similar deadline respective to fixed-price listings?[/q] No particular deadline with fixed price listings. Hopefully sellers with fixed price listings would have sold and marked sold enough games to get a table, and the few extra they might sell really do not make a difference. The main reason there is a deadline on auctions is because they need to close in order to be marked as sold by Nov for table assignments. Table assignments are arranged based on how many games sold (in an automated manner), and if a seller had, say, 30 games 'sold but unresolved' because of auction bids, they would not get a table even though they had sold many games. (This happened last year, and it was a pain.) To try to manually work around that for so many games would be very difficult. With a market this large, we have to depend on tools to gather the number of games sold, and to allocate table space based on how many sold. (i.e. so that it is not all bunched together.)

item.comment: Hi Nathan Wennerlind (Super_Satchmo) do you know which version of Carpe Diem this is?
It is the cover pictured… i know there is a particular difference in the editions but I don’t remember what those differences were

The first one had a star shape for the meeple movement, and then someone demonstrated to Feld that a circle was mathematically/topographically equivalent (but simpler to understand). So they changed it to a circle in the next printing. There's a neat forum post here on BGG about that.
Also the first printing had very similarly colored backs for all the tiles, and they improved the contrast (light green vs dark green) after that. But all versions are perfectly playable IMO.

item.comment:
I would like this for $3, cash at con
Thx! 😁
Hi Wendy. You still getting games for the submarines?

Thank you for asking! Yes still collecting small games! If anyone has a contact with the company that makes SCOPA (Italian card game with lots of replay ability) I’d love to have the information so I can write to them! Not at the same scale as I did last year…ALL 78 submarines (those are the ones we are allowed to know about) have been outfitted with “All Aboard Compact Libraries”! I have some being assembled “just in case” libraries (that’s what the commanders & I are calling them) to outfit potential “new” commissioned (or dark) submarines or if any subs need to “replace” a damaged library. These are being assembled and held until I get a commander request. Currently I ship 3-5 games to the commanders of the 78 so they can refresh & update their collections. They are also rotating the libraries from one sub to another when the meet up at docking. THIS IS THE BEST GIFT AND TRULY TRULY APPRECIATED BY OUR SERVICE MEMBERS! I HAVE HAD LOTS & LOTS OF FEEDBACK AND THANKS FROM SO MANY! I LOOOOOOOOVE DOING THIS MISSION!I 🥳🥳🥳

Cool. Okay. This one is yours - I’ll donate it.
At the end of the vfm I’ll gather up any unsold small box games I have and put a box together for you. Thanks for what you are doing,

Danny you ROCK!! THANK YOU THANK YOU! Please don’t thank me…this is truly MY pleasure! I wish I could win the lotto and give it all to our service members past & present!! 🥳🥳🥳 See you at the con! Want anything from Arizona? 🌵

No problem. Better with them being enjoyed than in a closet somewhere.
Thanks for the offer from Arizona, but I’m good. I’ll see you soon.
I agree with you! I pulled 300 out of my collection & sent them out to sea! I’m sure they are all happy too! 😎

So I was trying to remember why I bought this in the first place and how much it cost me and looked it up. At last year's VFM I bought somebody's copy of A Feast for Odin and they said they didn't have the promos so I went ahead and shopped around online for them so I wouldn't have to wait to add them to the game and the best price I could get for both promos was $50+shipping+tax. So I went ahead and ordered them and when I opened the game for the first time I found that the person who sold it was wrong and they actually did have both promos. Long story short, I effectively paid (after shipping and tax) over $30 for this promo. So there's no way I'm going to take less than $10 for it.
Makes sense. Go ahead and mark me down for $10. :)

item.comment: I'll take Sagrada Legacy for $15. Assuming nothing else was changed regarding the legacy aspect? I've avoided spoilers so I'm not sure how it works. Is it just the books you mentioned that get written in? Is it reset?

Each player gets a journal where each page is basically one play. So 2 of the journals have play #1 filled in. The other two are untouched. There are also cards and envelopes that get opened throughout the campaign, but we did not open any of them, so they're still new/unused.
BTW, I checked my box and forgot that I also have the booster packs, which includes all the original windows in a tear-off pad. So you could use the tear-off pad for play#1 for the two journals we used to be able to play 4 players.
If you're still interested, let me know and I'll mark it sold.
Sounds good, thanks! I'll take it!

item.comment:
BIN @ $300
This doesn't impact my buy/bid, but do you have the original boxes for the big box expansions?

Unfortunately no, Here is how I currently have everything packaged so you can have a better understanding of what you are purchasing. In the base game box is all the rulebooks, health dials, bits, as well as a 3D printed dish set and some chessex dice I used as counters etc. The big box contains the lions share of the cards while the smaller box is what I used to organize the active decks I was testing and playing as well as The parts of any campaigns I was participating in. When I would play outside of my home I would load up the smaller box as it has a handle as well as the base game box and leave the big box at home. I also failed to mention I am throwing in this third party log book for campaigns. Hope this helps!

I am looking for the base game and the Moon one…any chance you would break up this bundle for those 2 for $15?
Thank you kindly for your consideration. 😁

Hi Wendy. I unfortunately have sold Welcome to the moon. But you are talking to the son of a Navy vet. I will gladly donate this to you and I will go through my button shy games and toss in a few of those too.

THAAAAAANK YOU LOGAN!!! You are a very generous person!!! Please tell your father how much we honor him & greatly appreciate his service!!! My father was WWII Dog Fighter pilot and it means the world to me to be able to honor ALL our vets in following through with this mission - subs are TIGHT spaces & become a lot tighter after months under the sea during deployment and the submariners have really appreciated having games to enjoy during down time!!!! 🥳🥳🥳 Thx again!!!

Thanks for getting back. I think you've got the first printing. The product code for second is GMT 2325-24 and I believe it has the blue GMT logo. If it's first, I'll unfortunately need to withdraw.
Hey Duffy, product code on side of box is 2325. Copyright on the cover is 2024, logo is red.
I can offer $30. Open offer, please wait for others who can offer more!

[q="Munin"]Thanks for getting back. I think you've got the first printing. The product code for second is GMT 2325-24 and I believe it has the blue GMT logo. If it's first, I'll unfortunately need to withdraw.[/q] Just to follow up - I can confirm that the 2nd printing has a red, not blue, GMT logo on the box cover but the product code is indeed GMT 2325-24. The BGG and GMT Games images for the game show a blue logo on the box cover image, but that's not the case for the copy I just received.

item.objectname: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game
item.body:
SOLD LOCALLY OUTSIDE OF BGG
[-][b]Condition[/b]: Like new, everything sleeved since day 1 [b]Organization[/b]: Everything stored in 1 non-revised core box and 5 of the revised boxes with foamcore divdiers in place of the original inserts, the 5 boxes are the 3 sagas boxes, Dream-Chaser, and Angmar Awakened (except the player mat, which is too big to be contained by a mere box) [b]Price[/b]: $1000 OBO, open to a partial trade (send me a list of options, probably most interested in a complete Elder Scrolls: BotSE or something similar) and possibly (though less likely) splitting. Feel free to make offers of any kind as this is difficult to price out.
This is a giant LotR LCG lot. It includes all the revised content, several OOP expansions, professionally made MPC proxies w/ original backs to complete those expansions, and a custom neoprene 30x20" playing mat. The proxy sets do not include player cards that are duplicated in the 4 starter decks, and I think a handful of the truly worthless player cards.
Here's an easy to read list of everything included: - Full RCO (all the re-released content that FFG/Asmodee still sells, everything big and small) - Against the Shadow - 5/6 APs (Adventure Packs), the rest MPC proxied - Ringmaker - Voice of Isengard Deluxe + first 3 APs, the rest MPC proxied - Haradrim Cycle - MPC proxied - Vengeance of Mordor - A Shadow in the East Deluxe MPC proxied and the player cards from Challenge of the Wainriders - Various other player card proxies - Extra original core encounter/player cards if you want to make at home proxies - Custom player mat for 2-handed play or 2-players w/ threat tracker up top and custom cubes for 1-4 players to track threat and quests with - Organizer inside old LotR core box for 2 active decks and next quest with trays for the 3 tokens - Cards organized inside the 3 RCO saga boxes, Angmar, and Dream-chaser
For posterity, here is the BGG listings of everything that I have original, complete copies of (not proxies): [thing=349067][/thing] [thing=368767][/thing] [thing=394138][/thing] [thing=425071][/thing] [thing=382311][/thing] [thing=382310][/thing] [thing=359421][/thing] [thing=359420][/thing] [thing=415468][/thing] [thing=415467][/thing] [thing=357292][/thing] [thing=357291][/thing] [thing=357294][/thing] [thing=357293][/thing] [thing=350753][/thing] [thing=133167][/thing] [thing=134946][/thing] [thing=137773][/thing] [thing=139413][/thing] [thing=140917][/thing] [thing=146574][/thing] [thing=153130][/thing] [thing=154493][/thing] [thing=156416][/thing]

item.comment:
[-]Hey Laura how kid friendly is this? Kids Against Maturity[/-]
Doesn't seem like something after talking to some of the AP's that they'd want to have at the school. I'll keep looking thanks!

[q="Zafin"]Hey Laura how kid friendly is this? Kids Against Maturity[/q] Sent you a GeekMail. 🙂
For anyone reading:
Kids Against Maturity is marked for ages 10+ and is tame compared to Cards Against Humanity. There are a lot of poop/fart joke cards, references to gross food, school themes, etc. There are some cards that are seemingly innocent but could be paired in such a way that those who "know" will have a good laugh. For example, there is one card labeled "Squirrel's nuts" with a picture of a squirrel and some acorns... but if played with the "I saw mommy kissing _____" card (where the natural tendency is to say Santa Claus)... well, I think you get the idea.
We enjoyed it as a family because the adults still found the humor in a lot of card pairings, without it being lewd and inappropriate for the littler humans. However, I can see a group of older kids catching on to some of those clever card pairings and not exercising enough discretion around younger kids, so YMMV depending on age groups involved.

[size=13]$15[/size]
Relatively hard to find [b]Stefan Feld[/b] light-weight dice placement game.
A dice game where players have to place dice one by one onto certain columns of different anthills in order to attain the majority and score the most victory points. Majorities are not all the players must think about, however, as players will also want to place their dice on certain spaces to collect various items, forming sets that are also worth points at the end of the game. The player that is best able to balance attaining majorities while also collecting items will likely be the winner.
The funny background illustrations show the Anton the anteater in trouble with the ants and termites as he explores their homes.
Cash at con, or PayPal or Zelle beforehand.

Crypt is a small-box set collection game with a unique dice placement mechanic for 1 to 4 players.
Place your servant dice on treasure cards, choosing any value on each die. Choosing a higher value can ward off your opponents, but it also increases the odds that your servant will become exhausted. After everyone has placed their servant dice, everyone rolls. If you roll less than your chosen value, you lose the die.
Sets of treasure can be pawned off to collectors that offer bonus coins and special abilities. The player with the most valuable collection wins!

item.objectname: Kaosball: The Fantasy Sport of Total Domination
item.body:
2014 CMON English edition. Complete and in excellent condition - still in the shrinkwrap and suitable for gifting.
Eric Lang's answer to Blood Bowl. It's a bit more rugby than football, but don't let that stop you from gifting it to your favorite Cowboys fan so they can have something fun to do on Sundays twice a month when the Cowboys forget how to play football. 64 miniatures, including 4 full teams, and you can play 1v1, 2v2, and 3 or 4 v all.
[b]Mechanics: [/b]Miniatures, Team-based, Domination, Hand management, Variable player powers
[imageid=2568760]
[size=18]SOLD[/size] for $10 to [user=kristernevin][/user]

2008 White Wolf edition. Complete and in great shape. Out of print.
Remarkable comic style art in this one. Lots of unique illustrations all packed into a compact box sized perfectly for the components.
[b]Mechanics: [/b]Resource Management
[imageid=373044]

2009 English edition. Complete with cards in great condition. Box shows light shelf wear (whitening) along edges.
Fun John Kovalic cartoon art illustrating a 2-8 player space war card game. My boys really enjoyed making all the laser blast noises when we played this one.
[b]Mechanics: [/b]Hand Management, Variable Player Powers
[imageid=157567]

2013 Multilingual first edition. Complete with box and components in great shape.
Thematic abstract strategy game of elemental martial artists. When my boys and I played this, we always started with:
Water. Earth. Fire. Air. Long ago, the four nations lived together in harmony. Then, everything changed when the Fire Nation attacked....
Seriously, someone should license The Last Airbender series and reprint this game. My boys who played chess always enjoyed this one. [b] Mechanics:[/b] Action Points, Grid Movement

Fantasy deck-builder / area control card game where you can get your base wrecked by an npc dragon or convince that dragon to do the same thing to your opponent. 2011 Hasbro English edition. Complete with box, components, and miniature spaceships all in great condition.
Hits on ships are shown with pegs. That's about the only similarity between this space combat game about the epic conflict between the Intergalactic Space Navy and the alien Wretcheridians and classic Battleship. There's twenty surprisingly high quality miniature fleet and alien ships, an open space board, and ship cards with stats and damage allocation. It's a Hasbro game, but the design team wore a lot of Plaid Hats 🙂
[b]Mechanics: [/b]Action Points, Area Movements, Critical Hits, Variable Player Powers

item.body:
2004 Z-man edition. Complete with cards in great shape. Box shows some fading and wear, but is solid.
Build your own tableau of 12 cards through pick and pass drafting. When cards are played they trigger effects that may flip cards in all players' tableaus from scoring to non-scoring and back. The scoring is kind of like Fantasy Realm, in that it's based on the combinations of cards you have scoring in your tableau.
[b]Mechanics:[/b] Closed drafting, Hand management, Set collection, Simultaneous action selection
[imageid=170897]
[size=18]SOLD[/size] for $5 to [user=Aggie8709][/user]

2004 Histogame English/German edition. Complete with box and components in great condition.
Brilliantly designed game on the seven years wars, with Europe fighting Frederick the Great. Standard suited cards determine strength and movement abilities. You can play as Frederick against several opponents or as part of the alliance against him.
[b]Mechanics: [/b]Card play conflict resolution, Hand management, Secret unit deployment, Variable set-up
[imageid=3110655]

4th printing (which I think fixed all the misprints/errata from the first few printings)
Open, used - we played through about 50 of the scenarios, I think. Components are in great shape; all used cards are/were sleeved (we unsleeved and resleeved as we changed characters), and all stickers are part of the removable/reusable sticker pack. This is not reset but I might be convinced depending on the offer. I will reset the character boxes at least, to avoid the cool character surprises when new characters are unlocked (the best part!).
But, you get all these extra organizational components, which help immensely:
Four plano boxes with labels for all that cardboard! [imageid=9153120] [imageid=9153121] [imageid=9153122]
Business card holder for the equipment card market! [imageid=9153124]
Boxes for current characters (3)! Perfectly holds character board, modifier deck, action card deck, standee, equipment, character sheet. [imageid=9153128]
CD holder for organizing all monster cards and action decks! (We actually only used these for 3-4 games and then switched to using the Gloomhaven helper app on a tablet to run the monsters.) [imageid=9153133]
Extra box to hold all the map pieces! Also the reusable sticker pack is shown here. [imageid=9153136]
Baggies with labels for the various card decks. (Ok, this isn't that exciting but it does really help with organization, and as you can see we didn't permanently remove/destroy any cards.) [imageid=9153137]
I would LOVE to sell this locally in the north Dallas area and meet for pickup before the con, but I am willing to haul it downtown if you want to haul it back from the con 🙂

Players take on the roles of Quarriors - mighty mystical warriors who have the power to capture dangerous quarry from the untamed Wilds! They must conjure the mysterious powers of Quiddity, cast powerful spells, and summon their creatures to battle if they hope to overcome rivals and earn their rightful place as the Champion!
Quarriors has the frenetic excitement of a dice battle game, with an added ‘deckbuilding’ twist: players customize their dice pools during the game using resources generated by their rolls.
Quarriors takes the best of deckbuilding games without the tedium of shuffling. Take a typical deckbuilding game, add the speed and fun of dice and in 60 minutes you’re on your second or third game trying unique strategies against your opponents.

item.comment: I'll go BIN. I run a yearly Codenames tournament and I could use another game. I already own Grifters and at least one Phase 10. Of the rest there is probably something worth the money. The benefit of my being a noob in this rabid gamer community. My game collection has room to grow and I haven't reached the Seen That Done That state.

Bohnanza is a great game to play with several people. Jaipur is a wonderful 2 person game that is a oldie but goodie and never goes out of popularity in my opinion. Codenames is a great party game and Tiny epic kingdoms is great too , you are getting your monies worth . Oh you already know about Codenames. lol

The Tiny Epic Kingdoms is one I was interested in if I could get it for cheap. I've never played it, but it looks cute. I actually dislike Codenames, but it is very popular. I love to play in the game tournaments at a non-game convention we attend. The person running a tournament can't play it, so I run the popular game tournament that I dislike, and compete in the rest.
What a great Idea, that way you get to participate and play what you like as well.

item.comment:
I'll take this for $7. I was going to offer less but then I thought how I hate it when people nickle/dime/dollar the stuff I sell and hell, I'd be haggling $2 for another game that looks cute but I certainly don't need. Plus it plays solo. Because I'm a little short in the friends dept. I mean my wife is probably my best friend, confidant, and let's be honest, good in the sack ☺️. But she's more of a social gamer and PvP really isn't her thing so having something I can throw down on the kitchen table while she watches K-dramas in the background is really good therapy (I mean gaming, not so much the shows), and much cheaper than the REAL therapy by a large number of decimal points. It's sort of a mixed blessing, because I enjoy those shows, too (OMG Hellbound is an awesome series once you get past the first two episodes) and having the shows in the background is a little distracting but the biggest problem is finding an empty spot on the table amongst all the uncatalogued games, junk mail, and bills, some of which are in fact from said therapist...

Item: Dark Tower Condition: New Open Box...yes, really! Read below for details. Price: $200
Description What a rare unicorn this is! This is the original Dark Tower board game, 100% complete, with sealed components inside an open box. You read that right, a game from 1981 that has remained untouched / unplayed for decades. Because everything is sealed, the tower has not been tested, so please take that into account before deciding to buy. The box - as you would expect - is rough. The box was a stupid design anyway...the lid was not designed to fit snug, and there was a special cardboard insert (missing here) that kept the lid higher so it would be square. All four corner of the box lid have been repaired / reinforced with clear tape.
Inside the box are several still sealed plastic bags with components. Yes, that includes the replacement light bulb for the tower. The manual somehow got bent in the bag - the edge with the spine is curled up.

[b]Huge Red Dragon Inn Bundle[/b] Price: Let's Talk!
Sold via Geek Mail to [user=ir1337] [-] I did...a thing. I bought Red Dragon Inn. Then I bought Red Dragon Inn 2. Then 3. Then the Character Trove box (aka Red Dragon Inn 5). Then I traded for someone to get the special Red Dragon Inn cards that came from another game. Then I bought promos. Then - and this is where the insanity begins - I sleeved it. Everything. The sleeved cards got so big that I bought a second copy of the Character Trove box. And even that was not enough, as I use the Smorgasbox for storing tokens and coins and stuff. I wrote "make an offer" above because I am not sure what a collection of this size should go for. The entire collection is sleeved in FFG premium sleeves as well. So, if you have an interest, hit me up via Geek Mail or post a comment and we'll discuss. I am not currently interested in splitting out parts of this collection. It's either staying with me or leaving my collection as a unit. That being said, I have seen folks in the past that use the comments to divvy up a listing such as this. As long as the entire collection goes, it can be split up amongst friends.
I have many (probably most if not all) of the original character expansion boxes. I may or may not have the bigger expansion boxes (Red Dragon 2, 3, 4 and so on). The entire collection is stored in two copies of the Trove box plus the Smorgasbox and probably some of the base boxes as well.

item.comment: Hey Matt, per rule [listitem=12102319]3.2.6[/listitem] [q][b]Any Auctions must have a stated end date and conclude by November 1.[/b] Games must be marked sold by November 2 so that we know to assign you a table. I cannot monitor and contact sellers about 11,000 items. If I see an auction without an end date by November 1, I will simply delete your item from the list.[/q]

Sounds like fun digging through this and using for Warhammer Quest proxies. 🙂
$40!
Looks like a bunch of ork models to me, $30!
Thanks for the heads up, Jason! Fixing now!
Man, I just want to win and look through the box! Like opening a storage unit. 😀
Are these Warhammer Fantasy/Age of Sigmar? 40K or mixture of both?
I think they are Warhammer Fantasy mostly.
$125. Matt do we have an end time? and if so any sniping/bid extending options on that? Cheers.
I really want to be at the VFM just to see this get opened up. 🙂
I really want it so that I can give my Daughter a pile of minis to paint. She just got into painting minis...these would be perfect. I love modeling she loves painting.
In for $175. It's like the ultimate WHFB blind box :D

I hate bidding against myself but let's go ahead and jump it to $400. I've zoomed in on all the pics and it looks like most of a dark elf army and I'd love to lead Malekith in battle. Matt whether I win or not if you happen to have any army books/white dwarfs and any original empty product boxes (I decorate my office walls with them) id love to see about doing a secondary lot for them. Cheers.
This is the highlight item of the VFM! If anyone is interested in some painted Ironjawz, painted High Elves, Stormcast, Undead, or NIS Savage Orcs hit me up!

item.comment: Hi Ryan Kinnaman (RyansProShop) I'll bid $10 on Castle Combo.

The seller would surely turn down that frankly insulting opening "offer", especially coming from such an unreliable and sketchy character, but I'll raise it to a much more palatable $15.
[q="deitied"]Hi Ryan Kinnaman (RyansProShop) I'll bid $10 on Castle Combo.[/q]

I graciously teach someone how to play this game—basically handing him the keys to the "castle"—and what do I get? A passive-aggressive editorial in return and the pleasure of watching them outbid me on the very game I introduced. You didn’t just outbid me, you launched a full-blown ego parade with your overpriced offer and bargain-bin insults. Congratulations, you’ve mastered the art of biting the hand that tutors.

item.comment: I'll make an offer for this one of $150. I am worried that the app may not live forever, making the game unusable in a couple of years... But I would really like to try it.

It's a fair consideration. They've been good about maintaining it. Let me sit on it for a week or so and I may take the $150. It's an interesting game, and really a unique one. I just don't think it will get to the table anytime soon. :-(

I totally get it... and I don't want to undercut you by any means. It's just a high-risk purchase for me to try when it is so tech-driven. It seems quite unique and interesting, but it would suck to be a $200 paperweight in a year or two.

item.body:
Item: Shadows Over Camelot + Merlin's Company Condition: See Below Price: $275
Description I used Merlin's Company as the anchor for this listing as I figured it would get more attention. This bundle includes:
[thing=15062][/thing] [thing=35704][/thing]
This is one of two copies of Shadows Over Camelot for this VFM. 🙂 This one, however, not only includes the expansion but also the expansion box! And yes, the cards are (finally!) sleeved! It's a beautifully preserved copy of this decade+ old game. The base game box currently has the base game (sleeved cards), miniatures in their expected trays, and the dice. The previous owner was also nice enough to include a couple of fabric straps that make lifting the card decks out of the wells very easy. The manuals look brand new. The base game box has very, very minimal wear.
The Merlin's Company box has some extremely light dishing. I probably would not notice it but for my asking price I feel I owe it to the potential buyer to disclose anything / everything that would bother me about the game. So there's that. The white deck for Merlin has been opened, but never played. The black deck for Merlin is still shrink wrapped. The additional knights and the Merlin manual round out what's stored in the Merlin box.
I am not interested in splitting out the expansion and the base game.
Exchange notes: :arrowE: I will be attending BGG Fall. If I do not qualify for a seller table I will be flexible as to when to meet for an exchange. :arrowE: I am an experienced eBay seller and will happily ship games at buyer's expense. :arrowE: I prefer Venmo or Cash. I also accept PayPal Friends and Family once you have had the opportunity to inspect your purchase. :arrowE: I use [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/Condition_of_a_game]this article[/url] for determining the condition of the items I have for sale.

Item: Shadows Over Camelot + Merlin's Company Condition: See Below Price: $250
Description As with my other copy, I used Merlin's Company as the anchor for this listing, but a copy of the base game is also included. Specifically you'll get: [thing=15062][/thing] [thing=35704][/thing]
Merlin's Company has been combined into the base game and the original expansion box is no longer available. The expansion has not been played, but the white card pack has been opened. The black card pack is still in shrink.
Because the base game has been played, the edges of the white cards are clearly "dirtier" than the brand new cards from the expansion. Sleeving the cards should eliminate the ability to see which cards are clean versus dirty. If you hold up the decks (used vs. unused) you can clearly tell which cards come from the expansion right now. Sleeve your games, people! 😛
Here is a picture showing the edges of the base deck compared with the cleaner (un-played) Merlin deck.
[imageid=8465203 medium]
I believe sleeving these cards would eliminate this edge issue.
The trays for the miniatures have been discarded, and the miniatures are stored in zip lock baggies instead. Nothing has been painted. The minis for Merlin and Sir Bedivere are in separate blister packs rather than the zip lock baggies.
All of the dice are present, including the orange die for Sir Bedivere as provided by the Merlin expansion. The base game comes with 8 knight cards. Merlin adds 7 more (doubling up on all of the knights except King Arthur) to provide more variety in player powers. Merlin also adds, well, Merlin. 🙂 Merlin has a travel deck that impacts the knights as they attempt to travel from station to station.
The game box looks fantastic for something of its age. The game manuals have very, very slight imperfections. Enough so that I am not going to use the Like New condition, but maybe call it Very Good +++.

Item: Agricola Bundle Condition: Like New Price: withdrawn
[-]Description You may have noticed over the past few VFM events that I often list larger collections for sale. Case in point, sold everything Eldritch Horror in this VFM, and have a very large collection of Red Dragon Inn still for sale. I like to play games, but I also like to collect games. Once I start on something I tend to try to gather everything I can about that game, and take pride in being able to locate even weird or harder to find accessories.
Case in point, this Agricola listing. It includes: [thing=200680][/thing] [thing=43018][/thing] [thing=234218][/thing] [thing=247720][/thing] [thing=271144][/thing] [thing=329847][/thing] [thing=311545][/thing] [thing=210625][/thing]
But most interestingly, I have all of the different colored miniature sets. These are used to replace the standard wooden meeples from the base game. [thing=216654][/thing] [thing=216652][/thing] [thing=216651][/thing] [thing=216650][/thing] [thing=216649][/thing] [thing=216655][/thing]
Anything that has been opened is stored in the 15th anniversary box. [thing=370440][/thing]
I think the Farmers and the 5-6 player expansion are still new in shrink, but will have to check.
So, now what? 🙂 After all that collecting, I have played the game a few times (not my copy, generally) and I like it well enough, but I'm also considering moving on and selling the set that I have put together over the years.
But the quandary is that many folks who like Agricola probably already have some (or most) of this, so they're not interested in paying for the entire collection. And given the effort I put into collecting everything, I'm not interested in letting the premium bits (the miniature sets) sell separately from everything else, because if / when I do play my copy, that's part of what makes it unique. The Deluxified Dave experience, so to speak. 😆
[Edit to add] I have had several folks contact me about the listing, and decided I should put at least some idea of pricing. The character expansion sets are in my opinion the most interesting part of this listing. Each set can go for $30 or more on eBay or other places. There are six sets. That is before we add the base game, the 5-6 player expansion (which is also out of print) and the 15th anniversary box. While I don't have a specific price in mind, and would be willing to consider trades for similar value, I expect my ask to be north of $300. Maybe even $350. Or $325. Still figuring that out.
[b]I will consider offers that do not include the miniature sets.[/b] I don't want to break the miniature sets out, because if I keep the game I want to keep them. However, if you're not interested in the miniature figures and are interested in the rest, give me an offer. I can sell the miniature sets separately if I no longer own the game, and you would save some money on the purchase.
As such, do I suggest that you consider this if you are new to Agricola? Probably not. 🙂 It's hard to convince me that an "all in" bundle is a wise choice if you've never (or sparingly) played the game.
Bottom line - if you're looking for a very nice Agricola collection (way more than a "starter set") post a comment or send a Geek Mail and we'll discuss. 😎
Public service announcement: Cardhaus has the collector box on clearance right now for $25 so if you're just looking for the box, that's an option for you.
Exchange notes: :arrowE: I will be attending BGG Fall. If I do not qualify for a seller table I will be flexible as to when to meet for an exchange. :arrowE: I am an experienced eBay seller and will happily ship games at buyer's expense. :arrowE: I prefer Venmo or Cash. I also accept PayPal Friends and Family once you have had the opportunity to inspect your purchase. :arrowE: I use [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/Condition_of_a_game]this article[/url] for determining the condition of the items I have for sale.[/-]

William C. Dietz Book Collections. Both collections are historical fiction. The Winds of War series is about World War 3 using some current events to discuss how it could happen and then telling the story of the war. Each book covers a different theatre of war as he would see it playing out. Includes all 10 books in the collection in trade paperback.
$15 for the set
[imageid=9174984 large]
The America Rising book series is a post-apocalyptic military science fiction series. The three-book series includes Into the Guns (2016), Seek and Destroy (2017), and Battle Hymn (2018). The story begins with a global catastrophe caused by meteor strikes, which leads to the collapse of the U.S. government and a subsequent civil war between surviving military forces and a new corporate-led government called the New Confederacy.
All 3 books in the collection are hardback and excellent condition.
$12 for the set
[imageid=9174994 medium]

This is a bit of an unusual offering. I have a number of collectables, but I want to avoid having to list them on eBay, and deal with auctions, shipping, tracking, etc. I am just going to list them here. If you have an interest, contact me via GeekMail, and we can see if we can come up with some agreed upon pricing. I can also do pictures, but I want to see if there is any interest before I post them all so that I do not spam the list with photos. I am just trying to clear these out with the least effort. Since these are unusual, feel free to 'buy' them and I will bring them if I can fit them in the suitcase safely. Once you see them, you can feel free to not buy them if you don't agree it is what was represented. As I said, trying to go low key here.
If you are interested in any of these, contact me directly via geekmail. I would rather not get into a long discussion on the geeklist.
These are the general descriptions: * Apple collectable Developer CD Series: IV Disc Business, V Night of the Living Disc, II Phil and Teds Excellent CD, VI Gorillas in the Disc, VII Lord of the Files. ( Really neat covers for these, New) * Doctor Who Program Guide Volume 1 with Signatures: Nicolus Cortney (Brigadier), John Levene (Benton), Frazer Hines (Jamie), Jon Pertwee (3rd Dr), Janet Fielding, Antony Ainley (Master) * Large stuffed Minecraft Sheep in purple from Minecon 2016. It's the superego, includes: base deluxe, nightmares expansion (in shrink), soundtrack, association module and I had also added the holofoil cards. It was a 120 euro pledge. 70 is way too low. I've only played my copy once (base) and everything else is new.

I jump in and go $75, but that's my max and cannot go higher.
The reality was the SuperEgo reward was 90 euro on the KS campaign.
Since then It's been opened and played. Like all games that will knock a large chunk of value since it can no longer be treated as a new gift.
On top of that they are about to do another campaign run very shortly and will be offering the same game with updates and no expansions to bundle, so if this doesn't work for you, I'll just wait till then and get the new updated one unopened.

Bananine is a quick, mathy set-collection game where players compete to collect banana cards numbered 1–9. by designer Daniel Kenel (who made Gnaughty Gnomes, Dino Trix: Tarot Adventures, Big Wave)
Best Shot is a team-based trick-taking game for 2v2 or 3v3 players, themed around playing a round of golf over nine holes. Each hole consists of three tricks—the Drive, Chip, and Putt—with the card rankings changing each time to reflect the different types of golf shots. A team wins a hole by taking at least two of the three tricks, and the first team to win five holes wins the game.
Designed to make high, medium, and low cards all strategically valuable, Best Shot offers thoughtful hand management and teamwork across three tricks at a time. The shifting hierarchy of cards keeps gameplay fresh and thematic, though some players note that tie-breakers and limited team coordination can make outcomes feel swingy. Still, it’s praised as a clever, accessible, and uniquely 6-player-friendly trick-taker that smoothly blends golf and card play.

Cascadito is a compact, dice-driven spinoff of Reiner Knizia's Cascadero, offering strategic depth in a fast, portable package. Players draft dice to fill in spaces on their personal maps, connect towns, and trigger cascading combos for points. With four unique maps—each featuring different tracks, objectives, and bonuses—Cascadito offers a variety of strategies and high replayability, whether you're competing for public achievements or completing private goals. The game also includes a solo mode with varying difficulty levels. Perfect as a quick filler game or travel companion, Cascadito brings the challenge and excitement of Cascadero into a smaller, more accessible experience that's ideal for both casual and experienced players alike.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $15

Champions of Midgard is the ultimate blend of strategy, theme, and excitement — a Viking adventure that transforms classic worker placement into a heroic quest for glory. Step into the role of a clan leader, gathering resources, recruiting fierce warriors, and sailing across treacherous seas to battle trolls, draugr, and towering giants. Every decision feels epic, every dice roll a clash of fate and strategy. The game’s stunning Norse artwork, custom warrior dice, and smooth, fast-paced mechanics create an experience that’s as immersive as it is rewarding. With the Valhalla and Dark Mountains expansions adding even deeper choices and powerful mythic challenges, Champions of Midgard delivers endless replayability and unforgettable moments of triumph. If you want a game that captures the spirit of Viking legend while offering deep strategy and cinematic battles, this is your next great conquest.

Chock-A-Block is a bright, charming, and deceptively strategic tile-placement game where you’ll build the most delightful apartment block in town! Each turn, you’ll stack colorful room cards, attract quirky neighbors, and connect adorable features like cats, plants, birds, and even underwear to score big. Beneath its cute, compact exterior lies a clever puzzle full of tactical choices — balancing color combos to invite neighbors while chaining matching icons for points. With its vibrant art, engaging spatial gameplay, and quick 20-minute playtime, Chock-A-Block is the perfect mix of charm and challenge. Whether you’re competing head-to-head with friends or testing your puzzle skills solo against “AutoBlock,” this little box is packed with big personality and endless replayability. It’s smart, snappy, and irresistibly fun — the perfect addition to any game night!

In Chrononauts, each player becomes a time traveler, with a unique identity and a secret mission. During the game, players travel backwards and forwards through history, doing all those things people have always dreamed of using a time machine to do: Visiting the great moments of the past, peeking into the future, collecting up impossible artifacts and priceless works of art (at the moment just before history records their destruction), coming to grips with the paradoxes of time travel, and of course, changing pivotal events and altering the course of history itself. How would the timeline be different if Lincoln and JFK had not been assassinated? And is that the version of reality that you came from originally...the one you must return to in order to win? It's all packed into a fast and easy Fluxx-style card game that will take you to the beginning of time and back again.
Awards & Honors 2000 Origins Awards Best Traditional Card Game Winner[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $6

[B]Version:[/B] English edition (2025) [B]Language:[/B] English [B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]
designer: Maxime Rambourg (who made The LOOP, Dracula vs Van Helsing, Mind Up!, Big Book of Madness, Vampire Village, Happy Bee, Bravest)
mechanisms: deck construction, hidden victory points, take that, negotiation, party game
Step into a world of royal rivalry where noble families scheme, bargain, and battle for the throne! 🏰 For a Crown is a fast, clever deck-building and negotiation game that uses just a single shared deck. Recruit mercenaries, nobles, and schemers, slip them into your sleeve, and watch as the deck reveals each player’s machinations one card at a time. Over four quick rounds (about 30 minutes), you’ll buy cards for points, gold, or protection — or just to strike back at the leader. Expect wild twists, bold deals, and plenty of “take that” moments, but with a good dose of humor to keep it lighthearted. Perfect for 3–6 players, including families and casual gamers, it’s easy to teach, surprisingly strategic, and full of energy. Whether you’re negotiating your way to victory or laughing through the chaos, For a Crown delivers big fun in a small package. 🎯 Highlights: Fast, dynamic play — done in 30 minutes Smart blend of luck, strategy, and negotiation Family-friendly yet cutthroat enough for game night Gorgeous art and premium components Ideal “filler-to-gateway” game — zero bloat, max fun 👑 For a Crown — where every card could make you royalty… or ruin you trying![/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $25
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine. 5% discount on purchases of 3+ games, or 10% discount on 6+ games.

cover says "Free Ride" but it is dual language designer: Friedemann Friese (who made Power Grid, Faiyum, Friday, Fabled Fruit, Fishing, Fearsome Floors, many more!)
mechanisms: connections, contracts, network & route building, trains
Free Ride is a clever and approachable route-building board game set in late 19th-century Europe, where players compete to build railway lines connecting 45 major cities and transport passengers across the continent. With simple rules but deep strategic decisions, players must decide when to expand their own network, when to use or “nationalize” others’ lines by paying coins, and how to efficiently complete travel routes for maximum points. Every turn presents tough tradeoffs in timing, efficiency, and resource management, with coins serving as both a currency and a valuable source of victory points. Offering engaging multiplayer interaction and a challenging solo mode, Free Ride combines elegant gameplay, tactical depth, and the charm of European rail expansion — perfect for fans of smart, thinky train games like Airlines Europe or Ticket to Ride who want a richer strategic experience.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $25

Fuego is a fast-paced, fiery twist on classic trick-taking card games! Play solo or with a partner as you battle for flame tokens across rounds of clever card play, daring strikes, and blazing combos. High cards win tricks, low cards earn you more flames, and matching values can cancel each other out — so timing is everything. Steal flames from your opponents, burn bright to the finish, and be the first player or team to win two rounds to claim victory! With bold art, quick play, and hot player interaction, Fuego is the perfect mix of style, tension, and fun — an instant spark for your game night.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $20

Gachapon Trick is a colorful, fast-paced card game that mixes clever trick-taking with the irresistible fun of toy collecting! Each round, players compete to win tricks — but victory comes at a cost. The winner must spend their hard-earned cash to “buy” at least one of the played cards, representing collectible gachapon toys, or even gamble on a mystery toy from the deck! Earn points by collecting matching sets and managing your funds wisely — the more duplicates you have, the higher your score. GEAR is a bold and unconventional trick-taking game that fuses classic card play with auction-style bidding and open information. Each round, players start with two secret cards, then bid their victory points to acquire the rest of their hand from a shared market — but beware, those bids count against your final score! Once the hands are set, players compete in face-up tricks, playing singles or pairs in a tense battle of timing and prediction. Earn points for winning tricks, capturing special cards, or pulling off perfect rounds — but balancing your bids with your play is key. With its mix of open strategy, clever bidding, and dynamic trick-taking, GEAR offers a sharp, unpredictable challenge for players who love innovative twists on traditional card games.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $35
