mechanisms: tile placement, grid coverage, polyominoes
License to Grill is a light, family-friendly polyomino tile placement game for 3–5 players where backyard chefs compete for limited space on a shared grill. Players race to cook, season, sauce, and serve the best recipes—balancing heat levels, timing, and tile placement as meats and veggies sizzle side by side. Every turn, players choose two actions to manage their recipes through each stage, from prep to plating, all while adjusting the grill’s temperature to boost their own dishes—or sabotage others. With its fun barbecue theme, playful dad-joke humor, and toy-like components (including a real metal “grill” in the Premium Edition), it’s a thematic and accessible game that blends tactical timing, light strategy, and chaotic competition. Though some find it a bit fast-paced and repetitive, License to Grill shines as a quick, easy-to-teach crowd-pleaser for players who enjoy a flavorful mix of puzzle and party energy. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $30 Deluxe version -comes in red metal box that functions as game board with dials for the grill.

Octopus’ Garden is a charming undersea tile-laying puzzle game where 2–4 players compete to design the most beautiful coral garden. Players draft tiles from a unique 3×3 market—buying in rows or columns of three—to add colorful sea life and plants to their personal reef. Balancing beauty and harmony is key: attract seahorses and clownfish for points, protect oysters from hungry sea stars, and avoid scaring delicate feather worms. With gorgeous artwork, simple yet strategic gameplay, and multiple expansion modules for variety, Octopus’ Garden delivers an accessible but surprisingly thoughtful experience—easy to learn, tough to master, and perfect for players who love peaceful, puzzly strategy games like Calico or Kingdom Builder. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $45 Import

In Coal Country, you run a coal mining company, expanding your mine and selling coal to maximize profits while navigating a dynamic and unpredictable market. With a blend of worker placement, tile placement, and economic strategy, you must carefully manage your workers, who are assigned hidden values, to sell coal at the right time and avoid overproduction that can crash prices. The game challenges you to predict market fluctuations, outmaneuver competitors, and make critical decisions as you grow your company. With its unique theme, well-balanced mechanics, and deep strategic gameplay, Coal Country is a must-play for fans of math-based economic games and those who enjoy intense player interaction and ever-shifting challenges.
[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $7

Codenames is a clever, fast-paced party game of word association and deduction where two rival teams race to identify their secret agents first — without accidentally revealing the deadly assassin. Each team’s spymaster knows which of the 25 codenamed words on the table belong to their agents, and gives one-word clues with a number hinting how many words relate to that clue. Teammates must interpret the clue, make connections, and guess carefully — because one wrong pick could help the other team or end the game instantly. Balancing risk, intuition, and creativity, Codenames is a brilliantly simple yet endlessly replayable puzzle of language and teamwork that rewards both clever thinking and knowing how your friends think. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $5

Decipher is a creative and beautifully designed word deduction game for 2–4 players where clever minds race to crack secret words built from colorful letter fragments. Using the innovative Letter Piece Game™ system, players form and guess letters from just four basic shapes, turning simple wordplay into a fun puzzle of logic and imagination. Each round, one player becomes the “puzzle maker,” secretly constructing a word while others deduce its letters and meaning piece by piece. With every guess, clues build tension — will you solve the mystery or give points to the word’s creator? Combining the satisfying deduction of Mastermind with the wordplay of Hangman and Wordle, Decipher is a smart, family-friendly party game that rewards creativity, intuition, and quick thinking — all wrapped in striking, high-quality components and an ingenious box design. Once construction is complete, the twist begins — players swap their dungeon sheets, and opponents draw the path a brave hero will take through each dungeon, testing how well it’s built. As the hero fights monsters, springs traps, and hunts for treasure, the dungeon’s creator uses their cards to defend against the invasion — or sabotage other players’ dungeons! Balancing creativity, strategy, and mischief, Doodle Dungeon is part drawing game, part dungeon defense, and all-around hilarious fun for players who love fantasy, humor, and a touch of chaos. Dual is a clever and beautifully produced micro trick-taking game for 2–3 players where every card hides two celestial spirits — one Awake and one Asleep. Each round, players play cards from their fixed hands, following suits based on which celestial is currently Awake. But here’s the twist: the weakest player in a trick can flip their own or their opponent’s entire hand, instantly changing which suits are active! With mirrored card values, visible backs revealing opponents’ suits, and star-powered tiebreakers, every decision feels tense and strategic. Easy to teach but deeply thinky, Dual blends elegant design, bluffing, and clever timing into a cosmic battle of wits that rewards observation and adaptability. Beautiful, portable, and refreshingly unique — Dual is a celestial duel unlike any other![/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $20

Dungeon! is a fast, family-friendly adventure game inspired by Dungeons & Dragons, where players become heroes exploring a monster-filled labyrinth in search of treasure and glory. Originally released in 1975 and now beautifully reimagined by Wizards of the Coast, this classic dungeon crawl blends nostalgia with modern polish. Players choose from familiar fantasy classes — Rogue, Cleric, Fighter, or Wizard — each with unique strengths and victory goals. On each turn, heroes venture deeper into color-coded dungeon levels, battling goblins, skeletons, and dragons through simple dice rolls. Victories earn treasure, defeats can cost dearly, and the first to return to the entrance with enough gold wins! Easy to learn, full of risk and reward, Dungeon! delivers quick, dice-fueled fun packed with charm, tension, and old-school fantasy flavor. Whether you’re introducing kids to tabletop gaming or revisiting a childhood classic, Dungeon! promises an exciting quest that never outstays its welcome.

Evil Corp flips the script on heroism — this time, you’re the villain! In this fast-paced bag-building and tug-of-war strategy game, you take the reins of a monstrous corporation competing to terrify nearby villages and claim ultimate evil supremacy. Recruit goblins, skeletons, and mages to your growing horde, then unleash them to wreak havoc on towns caught between rival players. Each monster has unique abilities — some earn gold, others cast dark magic, and the strongest drive humans screaming from their homes.
With clever placement, timely upgrades, and just the right dose of mischief, you’ll outwit opponents to claim village seals and rise to CEO of Evil Corp. Simple to learn but rich in tactical depth, this game combines the addictive tension of deck-building with the back-and-forth intensity of area control battles. Featuring charming cartoonish art, tight gameplay, and endless replayability, Evil Corp is wicked fun for 2–4 players — perfect for anyone who’s ever wondered what it’s like to be delightfully bad.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $14

Fairy Lights is a charming push-your-luck card game about building dazzling strings of glowing bulbs to earn the most points. On your turn, you’ll reveal cards from the deck to add to the central “shop,” each showing colorful light bulbs worth varying points. Keep drawing to expand your choices—but beware! If you reveal two bulbs of the same color in a row, your turn ends immediately. When you stop (or are forced to), you’ll collect cards of one or two colors to add to your growing display. Complete sets of three bulbs in a color to score them—but collect too many without scoring, and your bulbs burn out! Quick to learn and full of tension, Fairy Lights delivers a delightful balance of risk and reward in a compact, replayable package that’s as bright and colorful as its theme.

Horrified: American Monsters is a standalone cooperative board game that builds on the gameplay of the original Horrified but replaces the classic Universal Monsters with creatures from American folklore such as Bigfoot, Mothman, the Jersey Devil, the Chupacabra, the Banshee of the Badlands, and the Ozark Howler. Players work together as investigators to complete each monster’s unique objectives before the terror level reaches its limit, using teamwork, strategy, and special abilities to save the town. While the core mechanics remain almost identical to the original game—collecting and delivering items to weaken monsters—the American Monsters edition adds slightly more complex quests and a fresh thematic twist. However, its muted color palette and low-contrast design make the board and components harder to read. Overall, Horrified: American Monsters offers smooth, accessible, and family-friendly cooperative gameplay that scales well in difficulty, making it a solid introduction to co-op games, though it may feel overly familiar to players of the first Horrified unless the American folklore theme especially appeals.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $15

Idle Hands is a quirky, devil-themed trick-taking game where players act as demons completing “missions” for their underworld boss, but with a wicked twist — winning tricks isn’t always good. Each round, the lead suit is set by a mission card, and the highest card in that suit wins the trick, adding the mission card to their hand. Most cards score +1 point, but 4s and 8s are worth their face value in negative points, turning victories into painful losses. The game’s special rules add tension and unpredictability — 10s can lose if multiple suits are played, and 1s can win if all cards match suit. With only forty cards, the game is fast, swingy, and mean-spirited in the best way, rewarding clever play and gleeful sabotage. While its chaotic scoring and “poisoned well” mechanics won’t appeal to everyone, Idle Hands stands out as a sharp, mischievous twist on classic trick-taking — easy to learn, quick to play, and delightfully nasty.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $30

I’m Right You’re Wrong is a fast, chaotic “take-that” card game that turns petty arguments into playful battles of wits and sabotage. Players draw and play cards each turn—using red Attack cards to punish others, green Highroad cards to help themselves (or soften blows), and yellow Trap cards to alter the rules mid-game. The goal is simple: stay in the game by keeping cards in hand and avoiding breaking rules, since running out of cards or making an illegal move eliminates you. Despite its combative theme, the game’s humor and self-awareness make it more hilarious than hostile, with bad hands forcing players into ridiculous situations and tough choices. Light, quick, and full of unpredictable twists, I’m Right You’re Wrong offers a funny, mean-spirited party experience where strategy meets chaos—and where being “forever correct” comes with a grin rather than a grudge. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $8

mechanisms: action points, contracts, delayed purchase, income, pickup and deliver, tile placement, drafting, network and route building, turn order Imperial Steam is a heavy economic and logistics strategy game set in 19th-century Austria, where players race to expand rail networks from Vienna to Trieste while managing factories, workers, and finances to maximize wealth before the game ends. Each decision—from hiring laborers and building tracks to producing goods, raising share values, and securing contracts—affects the tight economy and long-term success, forcing players to carefully balance growth and efficiency. Competition is fierce, as cities, resources, and opportunities are limited, making timing and route choices crucial. The game rewards deep planning, adaptability, and shrewd resource management, while punishing careless expansion or poor financial control, especially through its brutal share system that trades short-term liquidity for endgame penalties. With high production quality, massive table presence, and strong variability through randomized setup and city tiles, Imperial Steam offers a rich and highly interactive experience that appeals to fans of complex, near-perfect information Eurogames—though its lengthy setup, steep learning curve, and punishing economy make it best suited for experienced strategic players. Imwah is a two-player abstract strategy game that blends trick-taking card play with Chess-like movement for a fast, tactical experience. Players share identical decks of 11 cards across three suits plus two special cards and compete on a 6×6 grid to move two pawns into the opponent’s base or capture all opposing pawns. Each turn, players play a card in a trick; the winner of the trick moves first, but pawn movement is limited to the suit and rank of the played card, which dictates both where and how a pawn can move—mirroring the unique movement patterns of Chess pieces. The result is a clever balance between hand management and spatial control, where every card influences both immediate tactics and long-term positioning. The game’s compact design, chunky components, and tight, back-and-forth gameplay make it accessible yet deeply strategic, though the endgame can occasionally hinge on luck rather than pure skill. Overall, Imwah offers a fresh, engaging twist on trick-taking that appeals to both abstract and card-game fans alike. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $45

Jinja is a vibrant worker placement and area control game where players build shrines across Japan to earn honor and spiritual influence. Played over five seasons, players draft building cards, manage resources, and place workers on a colorful map to construct shrines that grant points and ongoing bonuses. Strategic planning is key, as limited building sites, variable goals (Omikuji cards), and seasonal events (Kitsune cards) create constant tactical shifts. While randomness from dice rolls, resource draws, and changing bonuses adds unpredictability, the game rewards adaptability and timing, offering multiple paths to victory through smart placement and efficient use of abilities. Featuring high-quality components, striking traditional Japanese-inspired artwork, and clean gameplay despite its many intertwined mechanisms, Jinja blends luck and strategy into a satisfying, serene, and competitive experience. Though its randomness and layered mechanics may deter players seeking full control, it delivers a uniquely meditative and engaging challenge for fans of hybrid Euro-style games.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $25

Juicy Fruits is a bright and cheerful puzzle-style family game where players manage their own tropical islands to harvest fruit, fulfill ship orders, and build businesses for points. Each turn, players slide fruit tokens—bananas, oranges, limes, pomegranates, and mangosteens—across their island board to collect resources, then either deliver fruit to ships blocking their shores or claim businesses that provide points or bonuses. Balancing when to clear ships for more space and when to invest in lucrative businesses is the heart of the strategy, as early decisions can accelerate the game’s end. Despite its light, friendly appearance, Juicy Fruits offers a surprisingly clever spatial puzzle with satisfying planning and timing challenges. High-quality components, colorful artwork, and simple rules make it accessible for families, while optional modes like the “juice factory” and solo variants add depth and replayability. Quick to set up and easy to teach, Juicy Fruits delivers a relaxing yet engaging experience that blends charm, strategy, and satisfying puzzly gameplay. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $13

Kilauea is an elegant, medium-weight strategy game where players embody Mo’o, lizard spirits from Hawaiian mythology, building colorful Tiki columns to honor Pele, the goddess of volcanoes. Centered around a rondel mechanism, players move their canoes around the volcano to gather Tikis from forests or construct them in either the volcano sectors or on their personal islands. Timing and placement are key, as the game’s dynamic scoring system multiplies the number of Tikis of each color in the volcano by those on your island, with taller columns worth fewer points but holding greater strategic influence. The limited “sacred stone” economy and powerful bonus actions add tension and tactical depth, encouraging clever combos and competitive positioning. As forests deplete, mid-game and final scorings trigger, creating evolving objectives and constant player interaction. With vibrant art, tactile components, and clean, old-school Eurogame sensibilities reminiscent of Knizia or Kramer & Kiesling, Kilauea blends simplicity, elegance, and tension into a beautifully thematic puzzle of timing, balance, and spatial foresight. Knitting Circle is a cozy, standalone follow-up to Calico that transforms the tactile charm of knitting into a clever tile-laying and drafting puzzle for 1–4 players. Designed by Emily Vincent with art by Beth Sobel, the game has players move their cat pawns around a colorful rondel to collect yarn tiles—each with knit and purl sides—to craft garments like mittens, scarves, and sweaters. Players manage limited yarn, match colors and stitch patterns, and complete garments to earn buttons and points while avoiding the dreaded “ugly sweater” penalties. With simultaneous action phases, variable goals, and advanced challenge cards, Knitting Circle blends spatial puzzling, color matching, and light engine-building into a warm, family-friendly experience. It maintains Calico’s satisfying tension but offers a more relaxed, flexible feel thanks to its dynamic rondel draft and combo-driven bonuses. Enhanced by adorable cats, rich theming, and replayable patterns, Knitting Circle captures the joy of crafting and strategy in equal measure—an inviting, brainy, and heartwarming entry in Flatout Games’ puzzle lineup. designers: Nick Fallon, Rob Harris, Kristian Amundsen Østby, James Sheahan (SPECTRE: The Board Game, Revive, The Magnificent, Santa Maria, Fallout Wasteland Warfare)
mechanisms: cooperative, dice rolling, real-time
Kung Fu Panda: The Board Game is a fast-paced, cooperative, real-time dice-rolling adventure where players take on the roles of Po and the Furious Five to battle Tai Lung and other villains from the Kung Fu Panda universe. Designed by the co-creator of Escape: The Curse of the Temple, it uses a similar system in which players roll dice simultaneously under a time limit—typically three rounds of a three-minute sand timer—to move, fight, and rescue civilians across modular, mission-based boards. Each die result represents different actions: arrows for movement, fists and kicks for combat, yin-yang symbols for healing or special powers, and claw marks that trigger random events or enemy spawns via each hero’s personal event wheel. Team coordination is key, as tougher enemies and obstacles often require combined efforts, and fallen heroes can only be revived by allies. Missions grow in complexity, with new environments, artifacts, and foes adding variety and challenge. Featuring custom miniatures, colorful tiles, and chaotic cooperative play, Kung Fu Panda: The Board Game delivers a lively, family-friendly experience full of energy, teamwork, and thematic fun that captures the spirit of the beloved animated films.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $30

Lagoon: Land of Druids is a deeply strategic 1–4 player game where druids shape the world’s destiny by exploring, harnessing, and unraveling magical lands infused with three divine energies—Elemeen, Vowelon, and Deonin. Each turn, players explore hex tiles that expand the landscape, choosing which side (and thus which energy and magical power) to bring into play, while also collecting “seed” tokens tied to those energies. Druids can move, summon, or activate the powers of any site their circle occupies, creating intricate chains of actions and combos. Players can also “unravel” tiles aligned with energies they oppose, removing them from play to shift the world’s balance and earn points. When the final tile is explored, the energy with the most sites in play becomes Lagoon’s destiny, and players score based on their support for that energy—dominant seeds and unraveled sites of opposing colors. Gorgeously illustrated and rich with spatial and tactical puzzles, Lagoon offers a “chewy,” brain-burning experience reminiscent of Hive and Magic: The Gathering, where manipulating the board and timing your moves is key. While the theme is abstract and the scoring system can feel harsh or swingy, the game’s elegant mechanics, deep decision space, and potential for creative strategy make it a standout for players who enjoy complex, thoughtful puzzles in a fantastical setting. 2014 Golden Geek Best Board Game Artwork & Presentation Nominee 2014 Golden Geek Best Abstract Board Game Nominee [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $5

Last Aurora is a post-apocalyptic, Euro-style adventure and racing game for 1–4 players set in a frozen wasteland after the Last War. As leaders of survivor convoys, players race toward the Aurora—the final icebreaker ship offering salvation—before it departs, managing limited fuel, food, ammo, and crew along the way. Over six rounds of five structured phases, players send out crew to explore ruined sites, scavenge resources, recruit survivors, upgrade their trucks and trailers, and fend off raiders, all while balancing exhaustion, hunger, and damage to their convoy. The game blends worker placement, resource management, and tactical combat, with players constantly forced to make hard survival choices—when to push forward, when to repair, and when to fight. Each turn tightens the tension as the Aurora edges closer to leaving, making timing and efficiency crucial. With beautiful art, immersive storytelling, and strong thematic integration, Last Aurora delivers a cold, tense, and cinematic experience where every decision feels vital. Its expansions and modular decks add replayability, and while luck influences exploration, success depends primarily on clever planning and adaptation under pressure.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $25

Last Light is a fast-paced, simultaneous-play 4X board game for 2–8 players where alien civilizations race to harvest the final light of a dying universe before the heat death of all things. Played on a rotating 3D board filled with colorful planets, players choose one of six action cards each turn—such as Mine, Research, Trade, Construct, Command, or Refresh—and then resolve their actions at the same time, keeping downtime minimal and gameplay brisk. Players explore planets, build extractors to gain resources, research powerful technologies, and engage in quick, dice-based combat as they move fleets toward the central white dwarf star. The first player to collect 20 “light” points wins, symbolizing the survival of their species. Each alien faction has unique abilities and tech synergies, creating strong asymmetry and replayability, while the rotating board constantly shifts tactical opportunities. The game is praised for its stunning table presence, quality components, and tight, hour-long playtime even with large groups. Though luck plays a role in exploration and combat, and its light 4X nature omits deep politics or prolonged empire-building, Last Light succeeds as a sleek, highly interactive, and visually striking space race that captures the tension and urgency of civilization’s final moments.

by designer Christopher Wray (Xylotar, Magic Trick, Kansas City: The Trick Taking Game, Rewind, February)
mechanisms: cooperative, spelling, trick-taking
LetterTricks is a clever hybrid of trick-taking and word games that replaces traditional numbered cards with letters of the alphabet across three suits. Players win tricks not just for points but to collect letter cards, which they later use to form words for scoring. In the competitive mode (3–5 players), the highest and lowest cards in each trick claim letters, and after all tricks are played, players arrange their collected letters into words—each letter scoring points, with rarer ones worth more. The cooperative mode (4–5 players) has players working together to form valid words from each trick, earning points collectively for successful combinations, while the team mode adds shared strategy and deduction. The result is a light yet brainy experience that blends linguistic creativity with tactical card play, offering tension between following suit, winning tricks, and optimizing letter choices. While it can be swingy if players end up with few letters, LetterTricks stands out as a charming, innovative crossover for fans of both trick-taking and word-building games, full of laughs and satisfying “aha” moments as players stretch their vocabulary to claim victory.

Longboard is a light, fast-paced card-drafting and set-collection game by Reiner Knizia where players compete to craft the longest and coolest surfboards to become the top surf shop on the beach. Each turn, players take two actions: draw cards into their personal supply, play cards to start or extend color-matched boards in ascending order, or trade cards with opponents by offering higher combined values to take a lower one in return. Boards score based on sticker icons once completed (four or more cards), with bonuses for having the most or longest boards and for meeting random objectives. Unfinished boards lose points, and players can end the game early once they’ve completed enough boards, creating tension between pushing for points and closing shop before rivals catch up. Blending familiar mechanics from Lost Cities and Keltis with a clever open-drafting and swapping system, Longboard is interactive, colorful, and easy to teach—ideal for families and casual gamers. While some find the random scoring cards and partially hidden sticker counts distracting, the game’s breezy theme, accessibility, and engaging player interaction make it a fun, replayable filler with classic Knizia charm. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $7

Loot is a fast-paced pirate-themed card game by Reiner Knizia where players compete to capture merchant ships and collect the most gold. The deck includes merchant ships (worth 2–8 gold), pirate ships in four colors (with strength values), pirate captains, and one admiral. On their turn, players can play a merchant ship, attack others’ ships with pirates, defend their own ships, or draw/discard cards. Only one pirate color can attack a merchant ship at a time, and captains or the admiral can trump regular ships. A merchant ship is claimed when it survives a full round or when a player has the strongest pirate force. The game ends when the draw pile is empty and a player runs out of cards, with scoring based on captured ships minus any unplayed merchant ships. Loot blends luck, timing, and tactical choices, rewarding careful observation and timing of attacks. It plays 2–8 players (best with more), lasts about 20 minutes, and offers simple rules, high interaction, and clever card play that make it both family-friendly and strategically engaging. 2005 Mensa Select Winner 1992 Fairplay À la carte Winner

Golem It is a fast, tactical ladder-climbing card game where players race to be the first to get rid of all their cards and magic tokens—but the tricky part is, you often need to take tokens to play your cards! Each turn, players lay down sets of matching cards that beat the previous play, boosting their values with tokens from a shared pool. Green (mint) golem cards gain +1 per token, while purple golems multiply dramatically, turning small numbers into huge plays. If you can’t play, you must return tokens instead—so managing both hands and tokens is key. The game ends when someone has no cards and no tokens left. Beautifully illustrated with colorful golems, Golem It combines accessible rules, clever resource tension, and satisfying combos into a compact, quick-playing experience perfect for 3–4 players who enjoy thinky, interactive card battles like Scout or No Thanks! Please Don’t Burn My Village! is a fiery, fast-paced card game of bribery, bluffing, and market manipulation where timing is everything and greed can literally burn you. Set in the world of Castle Panic, players compete to outsmart each other — and a fickle dragon — by offering treasures like barbarian axes, phoenix feathers, and king’s crowns at just the right moment to win its favor. Each bribe shifts the dragon’s ever-changing sense of value, making treasures rise and fall like a volatile stock market. Do you risk it all with a massive offering, or hold back and wait for the perfect moment? Featuring clever push-your-luck gameplay, dynamic player interaction, and chaotic reversals that keep everyone guessing until the end, Please Don’t Burn My Village! is an addictive mix of strategy and sabotage that’s easy to learn, quick to play, and endlessly replayable. Light-hearted, fiery fun for families and game nights alike — just make sure your bribe is big enough, or your village might be next! 🔥🐉💰 [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $14

designer Arve D. Fühler (who made Monasterium, Scharfe Schoten, El Gaucho, Festo, TA-KE)
mechanism: hand management
Pagoda is a beautifully designed two-player strategy game where rival architects race to build towering 3D pagodas for the Emperor. Each turn, you’ll play colorful cards to construct wooden columns, place ornate tiles, and unlock powerful abilities that let you bend the rules and outmaneuver your opponent. Every decision matters — build too boldly and you may hand your rival an advantage, hold back and they’ll soar ahead. With quick 20–30 minute games, stunning table presence, and just the right mix of strategy, tension, and elegance, Pagoda is a must-have for couples and competitive gamers who love beautiful, clever duels of timing and tactical finesse.

OPEN is a fast, clever, and unpredictable climbing and shedding card game with a bold twist — everyone plays with four of their six cards face up, and before the round begins, you secretly bet on who you think will go out first. Mixing the tension of poker-style bluffing with the pace and tactics of Uno, OPEN rewards sharp reads, gutsy timing, and a touch of luck. Do you play to win, or play to make your prediction come true? With its sleek design, 15-minute playtime, and dynamic mix of open information and hidden strategy, OPEN delivers a refreshingly social, interactive experience that keeps players talking, bluffing, and laughing until the final card drops. Perfect for poker nights, casual gatherings, and anyone who loves a game with brains and bravado.

[B]Version:[/B] Portuguese edition (2024) [B]Language:[/B] Portuguese [B]Condition:[/B] New - [I]NIS
Fel Barros, Mauricio Torselli (who made Dobro, Divicity)
Meio (“mayo,” like the condiment) is a brilliantly simple yet surprisingly deep trick-taking game built around balance and precision. Each round, you split your 13 cards into two “halves” — one of 6 cards and one of 7 — then play them in two mini-hands, aiming to win the same number of tricks in each. The closer your halves match, the better your score. It’s an elegant twist that turns traditional trick-taking into a fascinating puzzle of prediction and self-control. Quick to learn, endlessly replayable, and playable with a standard deck, Meio delivers that perfect mix of classic feel and fresh challenge, making it a must-try for anyone who loves clever, minimalist card games that punch way above their weight.[/I]

MATRX GIPF is the bold new evolution of Kris Burm’s legendary GIPF Project, fusing the elegant core gameplay of GIPF with the dynamic, power-driven mechanics of DVONN, ZÈRTZ, YINSH, PÜNCT, and TAMSK. This standalone abstract game reimagines the series’ signature push-and-align system by giving every piece a unique “Potential” — a special ability that lets you bend the board’s geometry, leap across lines, or stack in strategic ways. The result is a richer, more tactical, and unpredictable experience that feels like GIPF meets chess on a living, shifting battlefield. Perfect for abstract strategy fans, MATRX GIPF offers deep replayability, new layers of mastery, and an ever-evolving mental duel that challenges players to think three moves ahead in multiple dimensions. Whether as a thrilling standalone or an expansion to GIPF, MATRX GIPF is the ultimate evolution in modern abstract design — elegant, cerebral, and endlessly replayable.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $25

Matching 4U is a charming and cheeky card game that blends the drafting fun of Sushi Go with the tactical tension of trick-taking. You’re a girl scrambling to get ready for a surprise date, borrowing fashionable items—perfume, shoes, jewelry, and more—to build the perfect look and impress as many suitors as possible. Each round, players draft cards, then play tricks to claim the best fashion items for end-of-round set bonuses. With clever timing, light strategy, and an irresistible theme, Matching 4U turns every hand into a flirty battle of style and smarts. Fast, funny, and full of charm, it’s the perfect mix of cute aesthetics and clever card play that keeps you saying, “just one more round!” [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $30

Message in a Bottle is a fast, family-friendly word game that blends creativity, quick thinking, and tactile fun inside a charming corked bottle filled with colorful letter dice. Simply shake the bottle, reveal the letters, and race to shout out a word that includes them all—no need to build it, just think fast! With flexible rule variants, sparkling gem tokens, and an eye-catching presentation, Message in a Bottle delivers a refreshing spin on classic word play—educational, exciting, and easy to love.

designer Tsutomu Dejima (who made Trick-Taking in Black & White, TTB&W Hidden Numbers)
mechanism: trick-taking
Milkuro is a deceptively simple yet brilliantly clever trick-taking game where balance—not dominance—is the key to victory. Each card is double-sided, showing different values in white and black, and your challenge is to win an equal number of tricks in both colors. Too many of one, and your score turns negative! This elegant twist transforms every decision into a tense balancing act: should you seize a trick or hold back to preserve equilibrium? With its one-minute teach, smooth flow, and fast-paced rounds, Milkuro is a perfect filler for 2–4 players—easy to learn, yet surprisingly ruthless in its final moments. Compact, stylish, and refreshingly original, Milkuro offers a unique spin on the trick-taking genre that rewards precision, restraint, and perfectly measured play.[/I]
[B]BIN:[/B] $35 Import

mechanisms: deduction, party game
Mind Map is a clever, conversation-sparking party game where logic meets laughter on a two-axis chart. Each round, players secretly place their coordinate token based on how their secret word relates to two criteria—like “High-Tech” vs. “Old-Fashioned” or “Tasty” vs. “Gross”—while keeping a shared reference word in mind. Then, everyone races to guess which token belongs to which word, earning points for sharp deduction and clear communication. Designed by Gary Kim, Hope Hwang, and Yohan Goh, Mind Map takes the fun of Wavelength and So Clover! and adds a unique visual twist: a dynamic, discussion-fueled grid where every placement reveals how differently people think. Best with 5–7 players, it’s perfect for families, friend groups, or team-building sessions—especially for those who love a little debate with their data. Smart, silly, and socially illuminating, Mind Map turns abstract reasoning into unforgettable “Aha!” moments. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $15

Players work together to build an awe-inspiring jungle palace while secretly competing to earn the most banana points through clever planning, card combos, and spatial puzzle mastery. Every round, you’ll build colorful staircases brick by brick, earn Monkey Credits from your architecture, and spend them on powerful cards that fuel future builds or score big points. With trophy animals that add a touch of friendly sabotage and a palace that grows uniquely every game, Monkey Palace turns simple LEGO play into a surprisingly rich and replayable strategy experience. Easy to teach yet satisfyingly tactical, it’s a joyful crossover of creativity and competition—perfect for families, LEGO lovers, and gamers looking for something refreshingly different. Players draft their hands from open sets of cards, giving them control and insight into opponents’ strategies, then wager on their performance for the round. Mr. Lovenstein Presents: No Context is a wildly funny, fast-paced party game of absurd associations and chaotic deduction inspired by the hit webcomic. Each player secretly represents one of seven bizarre comic panels and must clue it in using other random panels—marking them as similar or different in some mysterious way. Meanwhile, everyone else races to guess which panel belongs to whom, scoring points for being clever (and quick!) enough to connect the nonsense first. Imagine Dixit and Similo had a snarky, slightly inappropriate love child—and that’s No Context. With its hilarious art, unpredictable logic, and endless replayability, it’s the perfect game for fans of offbeat humor, creative thinking, and seeing just how weird your friends’ brains really are.[/I]

Municipium is a hidden gem of Roman intrigue and influence—a sharp, elegant area control and strategy game by Reiner Knizia that lets players command powerful families vying for dominance in a bustling Roman provincial town. You’ll deploy family members across key institutions like the Forum, Baths, and Temple, leveraging their powers to win citizens’ loyalty, curry favor with the visiting Prefect, and ultimately claim political prestige. Every move is a balancing act of timing, positioning, and anticipation—plan too little, and rivals will seize your advantage; act too early, and you may miss a golden opportunity. With its rich historical theme, clever card-driven tension, and brisk one-hour playtime, Municipium rewards cunning planners who enjoy tactical maneuvering, interactive competition, and the satisfying struggle for influence. A smart, underrated classic that deserves a place in any strategy gamer’s collection. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $15

Myst is a two-phase puzzle and area-control board game inspired by the iconic computer adventure. Players, divided into two teams (blue and yellow), first race to complete their half of a jigsaw puzzle depicting Myst Island—each piece placed must connect logically, adding a layer of strategic puzzle-solving tension. Once both puzzles are complete, pawns move across the completed island based on spinner results as players compete to control key locations by overlaying puzzle pieces. The game’s strength lies in its novel blend of tactile puzzling and light territorial competition, offering a fun and fast-paced experience for puzzle enthusiasts or families. However, it’s far from the deep strategy of typical board games and does little to capture the atmosphere of the video game. Best suited for casual players who enjoy spatial challenges or friendly rivalry, Myst’s charm is in its hands-on, race-like first phase rather than its simplistic movement mechanics. [B]BIN:[/B] $4

New Eden is a mid-weight strategy game of underwater city-building, resource management, and risk balancing set in a flooded future where humanity rebuilds beneath the sea. Over three rounds, players bid, draft, and manage modules to expand their deep-sea stations while carefully balancing progress versus damage—pushing their systems for efficiency risks collapse at the end of the game. Mixing elements of Hadara, Spyrium, and Underwater Cities, it features multiple card-acquisition systems, oxygen-based worker movement, and a clever stability mechanic that forces tough trade-offs every turn. Though thematically thin and somewhat repetitive with two players, New Eden shines at higher counts as a tight, thinky tableau builder where every decision matters. Beautiful art, varied strategies, and streamlined gameplay make it a solid and accessible Euro-style game for players who enjoy resource puzzles and clever engine-building under pressure. Number Drop is a fast, addictive roll-and-write that fuses Tetris-style puzzle-building with clever number combos. Each round, players roll four number dice and one shape die, then “drop” the resulting polyomino of numbers into their grid—aiming to form groups of identical or consecutive numbers for points. Wild dice add flexibility, while “Drop Blocks” let players sabotage opponents by forcing penalty shapes onto their boards. Games last about 15–20 minutes, offering a quick mix of strategy, spatial reasoning, and light competition. With its retro charm, intuitive rules, and solo or multiplayer modes, Number Drop delivers a satisfying brain-burner that’s easy to learn, hard to master, and perfect for fans of Tetris, polyomino puzzles, and smart roll-and-writes.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $6

The accused must either admit their dominance (and lose points) or deny it (risking harsher penalties if proven wrong). Layered with asymmetrical character powers that let you peek, steal, or copy cards, the game thrives on reading your opponents, bluffing boldly, and pushing your luck. With beautiful but provocative art, snappy 30-minute playtime, and sharp interaction, Overseers is a clever mix of Sushi Go drafting and Coup-style mind games—accessible, tactical, and perfect for groups who love deduction and deception with a touch of flair. Pick a Pen: Reefs is a clever, family-friendly roll-and-write where players draft colored pencils instead of dice to chart underwater dive routes and hunt for treasures. Each pencil’s color and rolled symbols determine how far and in what direction you can extend your path, rewarding efficient planning and a bit of luck. With vibrant sheets depicting coral reefs, coins, and treasure chests, players race to complete routes and earn bonuses before the game ends. Port Royal: The Dice Game brilliantly reimagines Alexander Pfister’s classic push-your-luck card game into a dynamic roll-and-write adventure on the high seas. Players roll two custom dice to chart ships and wheels on a shared grid—pressing their luck for bigger rewards while risking a bust if duplicate colors appear. Each roll fuels decisions to sail routes, hire crew, and unlock island bonuses on one of four progressively challenging maps. Interactive and fast-paced, every player stays engaged by taking actions even on others’ turns, adding a layer of constant excitement. With top-notch Pegasus Spiel production—wooden components, double-sided pads, and smart design—this version captures the thrill, tension, and tactical choices of the original while feeling fresh and more accessible. As a veteran scout from the last human stronghold, The Fortress, you’ll explore a shattered Europe—scavenging resources, battling mutants, and reconnecting lost outposts through a mix of tile-based exploration, tactical combat, and branching story encounters. Every choice shapes your journey: mutations can grant power or doom you, and fast card-based battles keep the tension high. With over a hundred story scenes, evolving skill decks, and a richly thematic world, this is a true sandbox survival experience that rewards daring exploration and clever planning. Featuring deep replayability, modular maps, and a uniquely immersive narrative system, Posthuman Saga delivers the feel of a tabletop Fallout or S.T.A.L.K.E.R.—perfect for players seeking a challenging, story-driven adventure in a world where humanity’s greatest experiment may also be its undoing. Rajas of the Ganges: Cards & Karma distills the beloved dice-and-tile classic into a brilliant, fast-paced card game that captures all the charm and strategy of the original in a sleek 30–45 minute experience. Set once again along the sacred Ganges, players act as rajas and ranis competing to gain fame and wealth by managing cards that double as dice — using one side for powerful palace, ship, and market actions, and the other for die values and colors to fuel those actions. Clever set collection, timing, and resource management are key as you race to flip all six of your scoring cards by balancing glory and riches. With rich combos, cascading bonuses, and elegant card-driven gameplay, Cards & Karma replaces dice with ingenuity, delivering a masterclass in compact design that’s quick, tactical, and deeply satisfying — a perfect standalone experience or a portable successor for fans of the original Rajas of the Ganges.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $12

Born from the quiet chaos of the early pandemic, Rolling Realms by Stonemaier Games is Jamey Stegmaier’s brilliant answer to staying connected through play. This infinitely scaling roll-and-write game lets 1–6 players compete across a series of clever mini-games—each inspired by beloved Stonemaier titles like Wingspan and Viticulture—to earn the most stars over three fast-paced rounds. With just two chunky dice, dry-erase markers, and a handful of realm cards, Rolling Realms delivers a surprisingly deep puzzle that plays beautifully anywhere—from a cozy table to a cramped train tray. Each roll sparks tactical decisions as players juggle resources, tweak dice values, and chase that next burst of satisfaction. Its plug-and-play simplicity, high replayability, and expansions that introduce new realms from across the board game universe make it the ultimate “just one more round” experience. Whether you’re sneaking in a 10-minute “microdose” or diving into a longer session, Rolling Realms is a compact, endlessly replayable gem—a must-have for anyone who loves strategy in small, sparkling doses. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $15

[I]designers Tim Fowers, Jeff Krause (who made Burgle Bros., Paperback, Fugitive, Hardback, Now Boarding, Intrepid, Wok Star, Typewriter) mechanisms: action queue, dice rolling, grid movement, secret unit deployment, variable player powers, team based, bluffing, deduction
Sabotage by Tim Fowers and Jeff Krause is a pulse-pounding game of cat-and-mouse espionage where spies race to hack doomsday devices before villains blast them to oblivion. Played across mirrored 4x4 grids divided by a sleek screen, this team-based stealth strategy game turns deduction, bluffing, and tactical programming into a deliciously tense battle of wits. Each round, both sides secretly plan their moves with shared dice, execute actions like scanning, hacking, and firing gadgets, and leak just enough information to keep opponents guessing. It’s Captain Sonar meets Mission Impossible—but smarter, sleeker, and loaded with personality. With lavish production, miniatures, and a folding box that transforms into the battlefield itself, Sabotage is as much a showpiece as it is a masterpiece. The asymmetric gameplay, variable powers, and escalating mind games create endless replayability for groups who love strategy, deduction, and deception. Demanding, yes—but when played with the right crew, Sabotage delivers a cinematic experience of stealth, tension, and triumph that makes every win (and every close call) unforgettable. 3D printed holders for Galactic Cruise This post does NOT include the base game, obviously, just the 3D printed parts! This listing is for all of the 3D printed upright "rocket blueprint dispenser" and all of the containers shown in the top picture for the blueprints, nose cones, and engines that actually hold all of their respective cards (no more single cards laying on top due to the original boxes being too tight), and they still fit back into the original game box. The upright blueprint dispenser takes up less room on the table, and let's face it, it looks really cool. 😉Any of the blueprint boxes will fit inside the upright rocket blueprint dispenser section for storage/lid. The small rocket dispenser "base" portion may or may not store in your box - it depends on what's in your box.
[imageid=9196758 medium] [imageid=9196781 medium] [imageid=9196782 medium] You can see here that all of the nose and engine cards fit in the boxes. The blueprints fit similarly in their boxes.

mechanisms: trick-taking, ladder climbing
Sakana Stack is a clever, fast-paced climbing and shedding card game that blends the best of Fuji Flush, SCOUT, and Dobro into one beautifully thematic package. Step into a lively Japanese fish market where you’ll build stacks of seafood, outplay your rivals, and reel in big scores with perfectly timed moves. Easy to learn but full of strategic depth, Sakana Stack rewards clever play and sharp timing with satisfying, “just one more round” energy. Its unique follow-and-score system keeps every turn interactive, while the hand-painted artwork and compact design make it a joy to bring anywhere. Quirky, elegant, and endlessly replayable, Sakana Stack is the perfect filler game for players who love quick, smart, and beautifully crafted card games.[/I]
[B]BIN:[/B] $40 from Kickstarter

mechanisms: bluffing, communication limits, deduction, hidden roles, income, roles with asymmetric information, once-per-game abilities, semi-cooperative, traitor game, victory points as resource
13th Street Crew is a fast, flavorful social deduction game of loyalty, greed, and deception set in the criminal underworld of the Old Don’s city. Players work together to pull off risky jobs, earn cash, and climb the ranks—while one of them might secretly be a police informant sabotaging the crew. Easy to learn but full of tense negotiation, bluffing, and table banter, the game keeps everyone engaged from start to finish as alliances shift and suspicions rise. With its clever mix of cooperation and betrayal, cinematic mob theme, and smooth, replayable gameplay, 13th Street Crew delivers all the drama of Reservoir Dogs in a tight, endlessly fun package perfect for fans of Moonrakers and Secret Hitler.

Art Society is a witty, elegant, and highly interactive auction-and-placement game about curating the most fashionable art gallery in town. Players bid from a 1–20 pool to acquire paintings, arranging them in their personal gallery to score for harmony, framing, and prestige—while avoiding faux pas that can tank their value. Unsold works go to the museum, shifting the market and changing what’s “in vogue,” turning each round into a blend of tactical bidding, spatial puzzling, and gleeful sabotage. With its clever balance of elegance and chaos, gorgeous parody artwork, and deeply satisfying table presence, Art Society is a crowd-pleasing gem that rewards both sharp strategy and cheeky play. Perfect for fans of Cascadia, Ra, and Modern Art who like their euros with a splash of humor and a dash of rivalry.
[B]BIN:[/B] $25

mechanisms: area majority/influence, variable phase order, economic, worker selection
Nippon is a rich, fast-paced eurogame of industrial ambition and national transformation set in Japan’s Meiji era. Players lead powerful zaibatsu—corporate empires guiding the nation’s rapid modernization—by investing in factories, shipping, and technology to expand influence across Japan. Each turn, players draft workers from a shared pool to take strategic actions like producing goods, fulfilling contracts, or claiming regional control, but must later “consolidate” to reset their workforce and manage efficiency costs. Balancing short-term production with long-term planning creates constant tension, while timing consolidations and scoring rounds is key to success. With elegant mechanisms, deep interlocking systems, and a uniquely satisfying sense of industrial growth, Nippon delivers the best of euro design: tight decisions, meaningful interaction, and rewarding depth. Perfect for fans of Vinhos, Brass, or ZhanGuo who want an immersive, strategic economic experience that plays briskly yet feels epic in scope.
BIN: $60

Saltfjord is a richly thematic, medium-heavy eurogame set in a 19th-century Norwegian fishing village at the crossroads of tradition and progress. Building on the clever dice-drafting system of Santa Maria, it expands into a deeper, more rewarding engine-builder where every decision ripples through your growing community. Draft dice to activate rows and columns of buildings, send your boats to sea, fulfill trade contracts, and invest in new technologies to modernize your settlement. The puzzle of timing, placement, and efficiency is endlessly satisfying—fish double as both lifeblood and currency, while variable setup tiles, technology paths, and unique powers ensure every game feels fresh. With its beautiful production, smooth pacing, and deeply engaging strategic depth, Saltfjord captures the spirit of hard work and innovation on the cold northern coast—an elegant and immersive evolution of the modern euro classic.

Graffiti 6 is a fast, chaotic, and character-driven card-battling game where players use quirky animal gangs to fight for street dominance! Each round, players secretly choose and place cards from their hand, revealing and comparing them to outwit rivals. But this isn’t just about numbers—each team, from the Cool Penguins to the Crimson Cats, wields unique powers that let you freeze enemies, swap cards, steal hands, and manipulate the battlefield in wild, unpredictable ways. Quick to learn and packed with twists, Graffiti 6 delivers fast-paced, laugh-out-loud clashes perfect for parties or warm-up sessions. Outsmart, outplay, and out-graffiti your friends in this colorful, competitive street showdown!

item.body:
Version: Japanese Edition (2019) Language: Japanese Condition: NEW
designer: Hiro (who made Graffiti 6, Olenon, Double Nine)
mechanism: action/event, card play conflict resolution, set collection
Seven Vice is a lightning-fast Japanese microgame of set collection and sinful sabotage. Players represent the seven deadly sins, drawing and playing one card per turn in a simple Love Letter–style loop — but every card has a special power that can steal, swap, or disrupt opponents’ collections. To win, you’ll need to either gather all seven sins or four of one kind to score points, racing to three before anyone else. With its bold manga-style art, snappy five-minute rounds, and just the right dose of “take that,” Seven Vice is a perfect filler game — easy to teach, surprisingly interactive, and full of chaotic fun in a tiny package.

mechanisms: Area majority/influence, fighting, dice rolling, card game
The Coil is a gorgeous dice-driven area control game of power, strategy, and asymmetry set in a world literally twisted into chaos. You’ll command one of several uniquely designed factions—from the undead-raising Dedran to the celestial Celestos—each with its own playstyle and special abilities, as you expand your realm, muster forces, and wage tense dice-based battles across a shifting supercontinent called The Coil.
Over four escalating rounds, players build regions, deploy dice as armies, and clash for dominance, all while pursuing secret strategic goals that score points in eight categories. Every decision matters—when to strike, when to pass, and how to bluff your true objectives. With stunning art, deep replayability, and clever asymmetric powers, The Coil delivers a rich yet approachable experience for fans of tactical conflict, hidden scoring, and evolving maps—a standout indie strategy game that looks as good as it plays. Scram! is a lively, team-based card game of memory, deduction, and light strategy from Ted Alspach (Silver, Cabo) and Bezier Games. Your campsite’s been overrun by mischievous critters—now it’s a race to clear them out before your neighbors! Working in teams of two or three, players swap, peek, and bluff their way to the lowest campsite score, using clever card powers and shared strategy to outsmart the opposition. Fast turns, fun reveals, and the thrill of calling “Scram!” at just the right time make this a perfect mix of luck, teamwork, and light take-that energy. Easy to teach, engaging for families and casual gamers alike, Scram! is the ultimate campfire showdown—no bug spray required.[/I]

mechanisms: drafting, push your luck, set collection, variable player powers, card game
Shop Until You Drop is a fast, funny push-your-luck card game from Origame where players play as Singapore’s beloved Mr. Kiasu characters on a mad shopping spree to grab the best deals before everyone else. Over three shopping “days,” you’ll snatch up discounted items and try to pack them cleverly into your three shopping bags—each bag has strict packing rules, so one bad grab could make you “drop” a bag and lose your haul! Juggle percentages, colors, and chaos as chain reactions of extra draws trigger and send everyone scrambling. Complete Tompang (favor) missions for bonus points, and use your character’s special Extra Kiasu powers to bend the rules just enough to stay ahead. With its zany Mr. Kiasu humor, bold comic-style art, and quick, laugh-filled gameplay, Shop Until You Drop perfectly captures the thrill (and madness) of chasing bargains—making it a colorful, family-friendly filler that’s as relatable as it is riotous. [I]mechanisms: party game, betting and bluffing, player judge
Sounds Fishy is a hilarious bluffing and trivia party game from Big Potato Games where one real answer swims among a sea of fakes — and it’s up to you to spot it before you get hooked! Each round, one player becomes the Guesser while everyone else secretly takes on the role of either a True Blue Kipper (who knows the real answer) or a Red Herring (who must make up a convincing fake). The Guesser earns points for catching the Red Herrings — but if they bite on the real answer too soon, they lose it all! mechanism: trick-taking, ladder climbing, dice rolling
Tip of the Diceberg is a wildly inventive climbing and shedding game that fuses card play with polyhedral dice for a fresh, ever-changing experience. Each game begins by revealing a unique “diceberg” of meld types, meaning the legal combinations of cards and dice shift every time you play—so no two games are ever the same. Players race to empty their hands by forming clever melds of cards and dice, but once a meld type (like a run or set) has been played, it’s off-limits for everyone else that round, forcing constant adaptation. The suits are themed around classic RPG dice—d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, and d20—and dice rolls themselves act as wild, flexible cards that add chaotic twists and dramatic combos. Action-powered “dark” melds let players blow up the table or chain turns for massive swings, creating a tense balance between strategy and mayhem. While the rules could use polish, Tip of the Diceberg’s core is brilliant—a fast, funny, and unpredictable mashup of Nokosu Dice, Sumida River, and classic ladder-climbing games, offering a fresh hit of tactical creativity and dice-fueled excitement every time you crack the ice. [/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $35

Designed by Ren Multamäki and illustrated with haunting authenticity by Sampo Jumisko, Verdun blends historical realism with razor-sharp card play. Players command both French and German troops, forced to play cards that sometimes aid their enemies as they struggle to minimize casualties and protect their fortifications. Every decision carries weight—should you press an assault or sacrifice ground to preserve your strength? With clever mechanics that make every trick a costly skirmish and scoring that often leaves both sides in the negatives, Verdun captures the futility and moral complexity of war better than any card game before it. Simple to learn yet deeply strategic, it offers a sobering, meaningful take on trick-taking—beautifully illustrated, thematically rich, and unlike anything else on the table. For players who love games like The Grizzled or Bridge but want something more evocative and thought-provoking, Verdun is a must-play: a brilliant, poignant design where victory always comes at a cost.[/I]

But beware: in this game, winning a trick isn’t always the smartest move! White Hat combines clever card play with strategic positioning, creating a dynamic two-part experience full of tension and surprise. Its customizable boards, modular tiles, and variable setups ensure no two games ever play the same, while its compact, travel-friendly design packs endless depth into a small box. Outsmart your rivals, manipulate the flow of data, and balance your risks to stay ahead in this clever, unpredictable race through cyberspace. Whether you’re a trick-taking fan or a strategy gamer seeking something fresh and cerebral, White Hat is your next great challenge — a sleek, fast, and endlessly replayable battle of wits and timing. yea he does this every year he runs a normal bgg auction where anyone can buy and he'll ship it to you or to save you some money he'll deliver to bggcon. so it is in no way a part of the vfm other than using the vfm to get extra exposure since interests align
Fair enough. I got a bit confused since he offered pickup during VFM meetup time.

ah i believe he tags onto someone else as a helper and tells people he can be found there if i recall, been a few years since i did tables for november, his sales don't get him his own table.
A couple people tag together on these even if they have enough for their own tables just because they want to.

Makes sense. Makes it a lot easier if you need to step away from your table for a second.

As VFM Organizer, I cannot say I am happy about this. [-]You are advertising an auction that ends after BGG.CON which will be shipped, and will not be available for pickup at the VFM on Thursday at BGG.CON.
Please explain, or this will need to be deleted.
Buyers: Please hold off on this entry until I can get clarification on what is going on here from the poster.[/-]
The auction ends the 12th, bgg is the 17th. Just fyi.
I'll start the bid with $1 jeje

Well, he is tagging an auction outside the VFM which ends after the Auction cut off date to get a table at the VFM. This breaks the rules, and the seller did not contact me beforehand to try to get some extenuating permission. This is one more case of a seller pushing past the rules, which causes havoc with the BGG.CON team, can cause problems with buyers and sellers, and generally leads to a lot of hand holding that takes up too much time. This is occurring very late in the VFM, and it would have been better if it had been arranged sooner.
We will let it go this time, but be very careful in transactions. I will not be refereeing any issues here.

Monumental Duel: Trade is a refined, head-to-head civilization-building experience that captures the grandeur of Monumental in a fast, intense format for two players. Lead Japan, Mali, or Mexico through the ages, expanding your city, advancing science and culture, and constructing iconic Wonders—all while mastering the unique Trade module. Negotiate with powerful Free Cities to gain exclusive partnerships, unlock precious resources, and tilt the balance of power in your favor.
Streamlined yet deeply strategic, Monumental Duel: Trade keeps the original game’s brilliant grid-based action system while emphasizing clever card synergy, tactical timing, and smart resource management. Each civilization plays differently, creating immense replay value—especially when combined with the Espionage and Exploration sets. Beautifully illustrated and thematically rich, this box delivers a focused, competitive experience that feels more dynamic and thinky than 7 Wonders Duel, while still playing in under 90 minutes. Perfect for gamers who crave a tense, elegant, and immersive two-player civilization showdown.

Petrichor is a beautifully crafted, highly interactive strategy game where players become clouds competing to nurture crops and control the weather. Through clever action selection and area influence, you’ll gather water droplets, merge clouds, and decide when it rains—all while jockeying to trigger harvests at the most advantageous moments. Despite its tranquil theme of rain and growth, Petrichor is surprisingly tense and competitive, often feeling like “Diplomacy-lite” as players manipulate both skies and strategy. With stunning artwork, thoughtful component design, and expansions like Cows and Bees adding rich layers of gameplay (and solo options), this unheralded gem transforms calm weather into a storm of tactical depth and beauty—perfect for those who love elegant, nature-inspired competition.
BIN: $35. Base game NOT included; This is a big box trays storage solution for all the game & expansion content organization to upgrade it into a Collector's Edition. It does come with components for deluxe clouds and lightning bolts, and very nicely handy consolidated rulebook.

mechanisms: trick-taking, party game
Test your world knowledge and flag-spotting skills with Flagenius (Flag King) — the fast, funny, and surprisingly educational party game from Japan! 🌍🧠 Each round, players compare the hidden facts of their flag cards — like population, land area, or even the length of a country’s name — to see whose nation comes out on top. With 197 beautifully illustrated flags, you’ll bluff, guess, and learn as you play. Quick to teach and play in just 15 minutes, Flagenius blends trivia, luck, and deduction into a clever trick-taking party game that’s perfect for families, classrooms, and game nights alike. Who will rise to the throne as the true Flag King? 👑
BIN: 35

item.comment: I'll offer $80 for both Bloodborne expansions.
Would you be interested in a trade? Your Kabula Listing for both?

You won't believe this but I just realized I don't have the base game. I have the CARD game version... not sure what I was thinking. So now I am interested in these two expansions and the base game. I can trade Kabula and something else for Bloodborne and the two Expansions if you see something else to make up the difference.
Just looked through and there wasn't much else I was interested in. Would you do a trade & some cash? Kabula + 60?
Kabula + $50 and you've got a deal.
oh btw, turns out I have a copy for Forbidden Woods NIS as well. Didn't realize that. Would you be interested?
Sure, sounds good. I think that's a pretty small expansion. We can bump it up to Kabula and $60 again.

Forbidden Woods is another big box expansion, same size as Cainhurst. Adds two additional campaigns and a side mission (same as cainhurst), and just as many cards and minis. I'll counter with Kabula + $90 for the base game and the 3 expansions.

Now that we are 4 boxes deep into this, is this all part of a specific pledge from the original Kickstarter? Do you have the extras and other stuff from that? If I am going to go all in on this, I am now comparing to people selling entire pledge levels trying to get a handle on all of this. It seems odd for you to have just the base game and 3 random big box expansions if it wasn't originally a KS pledge.
I initially was buying the boxes one by one on hopes to playing years ago. Then got my hands on an all in pledge later. These boxes are the remainder from what I haven't opened and reboxed.

Okay, this is against my better judgment since it's not a full pledge, but let's do Kabula and $90 for the game and the three expansions. I'm in. Thanks for all of the back and forth. I appreciate it. Jason
Sold to Jason B for Kabula Bundle + $90. Now time to figure out how to sell these items like this...
Just realized, mb. The base game is not NIS, it is Like New. Opened but no pieces have been punched.

Version: Hot Streak ‐ English edition (2025) Language: English Condition: New - NIS
designer Jon Perry (who made Air Land Sea, Air Land Sea: Spies Lies & Supplies, Spots, Scape Goat, Time Barons)
mechanisms: party game, racing, betting & bluffing, deck building, drafting
Hot Streak is a deliriously fun betting and racing party game for anyone who loves the chaos of gambling on total nonsense. You’re not cheering for racehorses — you’re screaming at off-brand mascots in ridiculous costumes who might sprint the wrong way, crash into each other, or collapse in a heap before crawling across the finish line. Each round, players place bets, secretly rig the race deck, then watch in horror and delight as the mascots stumble their way down the track. With its wild presentation, hilarious unpredictability, and clever mix of luck and light strategy, Hot Streak delivers pure, shout-at-the-table joy. Whether you’re a hard-luck gambler or just in it for the laughs, this is one race you won’t forget — especially when you find yourself yelling, “MAKE THAT SAUSAGE RUN!”

Sold to David Cantrell for $45 per BGG message. thank you!

designer Dan Cassaro (who made Desperate Oasis, Fruit Boss)
mechanisms: connections, hand management, tile placement, team based, abstract strategy
Snakes of Wrath is a fast, cutthroat two-player tile game where cunning and chaos entwine. Build, steal, and sabotage as you grow serpents across the table — connecting heads, striking rivals, and flipping fortunes with every double-sided tile. One turn you’re methodically building your masterpiece, the next you’re stealing your opponent’s pride and joy with a sinister grin. With gorgeous, weighty tiles, elegant vintage design, and quick, addictive gameplay, Snakes of Wrath is the perfect mix of strategy and spite — a beautiful little battle where only the slyest player slithers away victorious.

Version: Formaggio ‐ English edition (2025) Language: English Condition: New - NIS
designer Ben Rosset (who made Fromage, Search From Planet X, Between Two Cities, Brew Crafters, Search for Lost Species, Between Two Castles of Mad King Ludwig, First in Flight, The Game Makers)
mechanisms: chaining, drafting, contracts, end game bonuses, rondel, set collection, worker placement
Step into the golden age of Italian cheesemaking in Formaggio, a standalone expansion for Fromage where players simultaneously place workers to craft, age, and sell their artisanal cheeses. Each round, you’ll gather resources, manage your creamery, and then rotate the board—aging your cheeses and revealing fresh opportunities in a new quadrant. Master the unique challenges of four new regions: pair your cheeses with fine wines in the Vigneto, serve demanding diners along the Venetian canals, distribute your goods across Italy’s Regioni, and even secure loans with cheese at the Banca. With platinum-tier cheeses, seasonal bonuses, and new player abilities, Formaggio deepens the strategic puzzle of worker placement and timing—offering endlessly satisfying layers of flavor for fans of elegant, interactive Euro-style gameplay.
Formaggio Limited Edition from the Kickstarter: [B]BIN:[/B] $70 Limited Edition content includes: --108 Wood Tokens upgrade the punchboard tokens (which are different from the shapes in Fromage) --Premium Neoprene Mat with durable stitched edges and new form factor for better board support. Plus, it fits in the box without crimping. --The New Twist-Lock Axle keeps the rotating board perfectly flush and centered, ensuring an ultra-smooth rotation with a simple one-finger push.
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine. 5% discount on purchases of 3+ games, or 10% discount on 6+ games.

item.body:
Version: 7 Wonders: Manneken Pis ‐ English edition (2021) condition: Like New
7 Wonders: Manneken Pis – first available as a promotional item at Spiel 2010, then distributed later via the BGG Store and Spielbox – is a wonder that can be used with the 7 Wonders base game in order for players to have more choices of wonders available to them.
Unlike the wonders included with the base game, Manneken Pis produces no resource of its own, instead giving its owner more money at the start of the game. One side of this wonder allows its owner to copy specific levels found on neighboring wonder cards, while the other side consists of a single level that requires one of each resource for a single huge payoff in power, points, and the purse.
[B]BIN:[/B] $5 - promo for 7 Wonders
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine.

Age of Innovation: Faction Enhancement Pack ‐ English edition (2025) condition: new
Includes errata for Illusionists, Navigators, Moles. 1) Illusionists: Instead of giving 3 points with 2-4 players or 4 points with 5 players, they give 1 point with 2-3 players or 2 points with 4-5 players when using a power action. 2) Navigators: In addition to giving 2 points, they also give 1 money whenever they build next to a river space. 3) Moles: Instead of giving 4 points whenever they use their ability, they gain 2 points plus 1 point per player in the game.
The Age of Innovation Enhancement Pack contains 3 modified factions to provide better balance within the game. Modified factions include: Moles, Illusionists, and Navigators.
[B]BIN:[/B] $10 - accessory for Age of Innovation - NOT the base game.
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine.

item.objectname: Eaten By Zombies!: We Have the Bomb! Promo
item.body:
Eaten By Zombies!: We Have the Bomb! Promo (English edition) condition: new
Hay, look what you found! It’s a safe cozy shelter to hide from all those pesky zombies outside… but what if you have a Bomb Shelter then who has their finger on the BOMB! With the 'We have the Bomb!' promo pack the ante has just been upped. Now you don’t just have zombies to worry about because now someone is about to drop a bomb shell on them! You and the other survivors are about to become collateral damage … you better hope you have a shelter in that Safe House of yours! The 'We have the Bomb!' promo comes with 9 cards; 8 'Bomb Shelters' Swag cards to add to any game of Eaten by zombies! & 1 'We have the Bomb!' a unique card that will be added to the bottom ten cards of the 'Zombie Deck' to be dropped on all the Survivors and Zombies at the same time.
[B]BIN:[/B] $3 - promo for Eaten by Zombies
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine.

mechanisms: auction/bidding, set collection, humor
Step into a world of magical mayhem with Elixir, the hilarious card game where mischievous fairies and wizards race to gather whimsical ingredients, cast outrageous spells, and hex their friends into laughter! Easy to learn and bursting with charm, Elixir blends light strategy with riotous party fun—one moment you’re stealing potions, the next you’re forced to call another player “Master” or shout “Well, I’ll be a monkey’s uncle!” every time you speak. With gorgeous storybook artwork and endless replayability, Elixir is the perfect recipe for an enchanting, laugh-out-loud game night. Whether you’re a seasoned gamer or just love a bit of magical mischief, Elixir will have your whole table under its spel

item.body:
Francis Drake: Montezuma's Legacy Expansion (English edition) 2013 condition: new
In the game Francis Drake, the players are in the Elizabethan era in the attempting to emulate the legend of Sir Francis Drake, hero to the English but a pirate to the Spanish. After the set up, each player must chart a course toward the riches of the Aztec and Incan Empires and complete 3 missions.
Montezuma's Legacy is an Expansion to replace the Spanish Galleons and the Jewel accompanying the Spanish Galleon. The Jewel is replaced on each voyage with the Aztec Relic. If a galleon is captured, the relic goes in the player's treasure chest and it's scored at the end of the game.

item.body:
Galileo Galilei: Edmond Halley Promo (English edition) 2024 condition: new
Enhance your base game by adding the Edmond Halley character. Utilize his unique comet ability to make the advanced game mode even more dynamic and challenging!
Halley has three personal comet spaces and one special comet tile. The comet spaces are: - give a lecturers gain one quadrant - increase two of your dice by 3 - gain 7 points
Halley’s Comet as two attributes. It has value 2 on the starting side and value 3 on the flipped side. You use it the same way as other comets while observing. When you use it for the second time you may place it on your personal comet spaces or on the home board. When you trigger a "spot a comet" action, you may use this comet instead of one on your player board. This allows you to use this comet multiple times. Once you take it from a comet space it was placed on, the reward on it becomes available again. This applies even for your personal comet pages.
[B]BIN:[/B] $15

item.objectname: Jet Set: Distant Lands – Expansion Set 1
item.body:
Jet Set: Distant Lands – Expansion Set 1 (Multilingual first edition) 2010 condition: new - Part of corner is dinged 1 cm. Can send a photo. (This expansion contents fits inside base game box however.)
Jet Set: Distant Lands - Expansion Set 1 is a set of expansions for Jet Set (including the Jet Set: Investor & Business Expansion, which was previously released alone) adding four new ways to play the game as well as 90 more Long and Short Flight Cards and 18 more Final Flight Cards. You can add the expansions individually or combine them for more fun:
Flight cards Short Flight Cards (50 cards) - adds more Short Flight options Long Flight Cards (40 cards) - adds more Long Flight options Final Flight Cards (18 cards) - adds more Final Flight options Investor (8 cards) - injects money when Vacation cards are drawn based upon conditions mentioned on the card - e.g. receive €2 for each VP Business (40 cards) - allowing you to bend the rules - e.g. by placing free planes, by locking down an unclaimed Flight Card or by collecting tax money from the other players' income Hubs (plastic hub markers, die-cut tokens for VP bonuses and income bonuses) - adds bonuses for routing flights through certain cities Distant Lands (two small boards, a deck of International flights cards, 12 city tokens) - adds Intercontinental flights which are expensive but gives a good boost to income and VP
[B]BIN:[/B] $10 - expansion to Jet Set
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine.
