item.objectname: Let's Go! To Japan: Day Trip
item.body:
Let's Go! To Japan: Day Trip ‐ English edition (2024) condition: new
Let's Go! To Japan: Day Trip allows players to visit cities one of 10 other cities in Japan outside of Tokyo and Kyoto. Will you eat amazing street food in Osaka, visit the castle ruins of Fukuoka, or will you feed the bowing deer of Nara?
The Day Trip expansion adds 12 Day Trip cards which give players additional goals allowing for even more strategic decisions and adds Sunday to the game. Players can freely move Sunday between the start and end of their vacation.
It’s difficult to see all the cities you want to go to in a single trip. Sometimes taking a day trip can be an amazing way to see a nearby city without complicating your itinerary. Let’s Go! To Japan: Day Trip allows players to visit one of 10 other cities in Japan. Will you eat amazing street food in Osaka, visit the Castle ruins of Fukuoka, or will you feed the bowing deer of Nara?
[B]BIN:[/B] $13 - expansion to Let's Go to Japan
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine.

Metrorunner: Dropsite Mini Expansion (English edition) 2024 condition: new
This mini expansion for Metrorunner offers a new path to earning points as you navigate the districts of Mirror City! Pick up a quick mission and run it to a destination on the board to earn a bonus. The more drops you deliver, the more points you'll earn at the end of the game.
Incudes: 15 Dropsite cards and 2 rules cards.
Gameplay: When a player ends their movement on a location with a dropsite card, they may take the card and place it face up near their runner board. This is a free action. Then, immediately reveal a new Dropsite card (face up) on the board in the correct location. Each player may only have one face up Dropsite card at a time. When a player with a face-up Dropsite card ends their movement on the Dropsite (the location on the right side of the card), they flip the Dropsite card over. Scoring: During final scoring, earn points based on the number of face-down Dropsite cards. Solo mode: If a rogue token ever shares a location with a Dropsite card, discard is and reveal a new one.
[B]BIN:[/B] $10 - expansion to Metrorunner
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine.

item.objectname: Punderdome: A Card Game for Pun Lovers
item.body:
Punderdome: A Card Game for Pun Lovers (English edition) condition: very good
Punderdome is a fast-paced party game that celebrates terrible puns and quick wit. Each round, one player draws two prompt cards (like Breakfast and Zombies), and everyone else has 90 seconds to mash them into the funniest pun they can. Players share their creations, the judge picks a winner, and the first to collect 10 winning pairs takes the crown. It’s easy to learn, hilarious in groups, and perfect for pun enthusiasts, improv fans, and anyone who loves to laugh at how bad a joke can be.
[B]BIN:[/B] $3
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine.

[q="sbakerj"]For Adrienne's benefit:
Rule 3.2.7, if you've agreed to the sale you must follow through[/q] It's $3. People make mistakes. I had someone buy a $45 game from me and then backed out because they already had the game apparently. I took the hit, because accidents happen. I have also probably sold something that I thought I had the inventory for and realized I didn't. Mistakes happen.

I'm not sure what that means. I'm not going to force someone to either buy the game and sell it to me for $3 or give me money to "reimburse" me for a game they don't have. No money or goods have been exchanged so cancellation seems like a perfectly acceptable option to me. Everyone makes mistakes and I would really hope that most or all of the people selling & buying on here are doing so in good faith.

You would hope people would be sensible, sadly, there have been issues in the past that have caused for such rules to be put in place. If seller and buyer are cool with it, no reason for anything to be enforced. I believe the rule is in place when there is a disagreement.
thank you for your kindness and understanding

Version: English edition (2025) Language: English Condition: New - NIS
designer Taylor Reiner (who made Seers Catalog, Of What's Left, Short Zoot Suit, Sail Legacy, Chai Tea Jazz)
mechanism: trick-taking
Tricky Twist flips traditional trick-taking on its head, rewarding clever losses as much as wins. When you can’t follow suit, your card returns as a “false trick,” which can score big when balanced and sequenced with your true tricks. Winning a 7 unlocks bonus cards with powerful effects, while rotating scoring cards keep each round fresh and strategic. A refined version of Short Zoot Suit with new artwork, expanded scoring, and added depth, Tricky Twist is a fast, 25-minute game for 3–4 players where smart timing and calculated risk make losing feel like winning. It’s a delightfully tricky puzzle of precision, planning, and playful misdirection.
[B]BIN:[/B] $35
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine. 5% discount on purchases of 3+ games, or 10% discount on 6+ games.

Version: Tsumooo! (English/Japanese edition) 2025 Condition: new - NIS
mechanism: trick-taking
Tsumooo! is a fast, chaotic trick-taking game built around the “Law of Universal Draw,” where every card you play forces you to draw from mysterious piles created by other players. Before the round begins, everyone secretly loads these draw decks with traps or opportunities, making each draw a mind game of risk and prediction. As you try to hit your bid, you’ll read opponents’ intentions, guess which stacks hold strength or weakness, and adapt as your hand constantly evolves. It’s clever, unpredictable, and surprisingly strategic — blending bluffing, psychology, and beautiful art into one compact, inventive card game.
[B]BIN:[/B] $35

Sweet & Spicy ‐ English edition (2022) condition: new
designer Győri Zoltán Gábor (who made Spicy)
mechanisms: hand management, bluffing
Sweet & Spicy is a charming bluffing card game for 2–6 players by Győri Zoltán Gábor and HeidelBÄR Games, blending sugary sweetness with a dash of playful heat. Illustrated by Yoon Sung, its adorable kittens hide fierce competitive spirits as players play cards facedown, declaring numbers and spices — truth or bluff — while others can challenge only one detail, making even half-truths clever plays. A family-friendly reimagining of Spicy, it replaces Wasabi with Lemon, adds the all-powerful Super Joker, and softens the edges for kids and casual gamers without losing the fun. Easy to learn, quick to play, and delightfully mischievous, Sweet & Spicy keeps families laughing, bluffing, and meowing for one more round.

item.body:
TAGS ‐ English edition (2018) condition: new
designer Spartaco Albertarelli (who made Coyote, VektoRace, Dust, Kaleidos)
TAGS is a fast, zany word game where players have just 15 seconds to blurt out words that match both a letter and a topic—say “Firefighter” for “Jobs” and “F,” grab the marble, and rack up points before time runs out. A modern reimagining of the 1995 game Category, it blends the pressure of Scattergories with tactile fun as players snatch marbles from a colorful board. Quick to teach and endlessly replayable with thousands of letter-and-topic combos, TAGS scales from 2–4 players or up to 12 in teams, keeping everyone laughing, debating, and thinking fast in this energetic, family-friendly word showdown.

item.body:
Uninvited Guests at a Wedding (English edition) 2025 condition: new - NIS Import
mechanisms: bluffing, deduction, party game, events, hidden roles
Uninvited Guests at a Wedding – You may not have been on the guest list, but you couldn’t resist the irresistible lure of free food, loud music, and chaotic fun! In this fast-paced hidden-role and bluffing game, players crash an extravagant Indian wedding and must erase photographic evidence, shift suspicion, and accuse their friends before getting caught by nosy aunties. Every turn is a tense dance between risk and revelation — clear evidence to protect yourself or point the finger to expose another gatecrasher. With quick rounds, hilarious banter, and a wildly thematic setting full of color and chaos, Uninvited Guests at a Wedding is the perfect party game for groups that love deduction, misdirection, and a dash of drama worthy of a Bollywood finale.
BIN $30

Version: Captains of the Gulf ‐ English/German edition (2021) Condition: Like New
designer Jason Dinger (who also made Crescent City Cargo)
mechanisms: hand management, multi-use cards, pickup and deliver, economic
Captains of the Gulf casts players as shrimp-boat captains navigating the Gulf of Mexico, juggling fishing licenses, crew, and boat upgrades while trying to turn the biggest profit from catches of shrimp, crabs, and oysters. Using a clever rondel action system and multi-use cards, every decision becomes a trade-off between upgrading your operation, spending fuel to reach the best fishing spots, or cashing in your haul at port—where timing and market demand can make or break your fortune. Thematically rich and mechanically elegant, it blends economic management, route planning, and hand optimization into a satisfyingly strategic experience that rewards foresight and efficiency. While its pace can feel deliberate, fans praise its grounded realism, deep replayability, and authentic portrayal of life on the Gulf, making it a hidden gem among heavier euro-style games.
[B]BIN:[/B] $25

$10. Brand New. NIS. Fromage Lazy Susan Upgrade.
Neoprene mat, center piece that holds the boards together, and center resource selection board for Fromage. The center piece holds it together well so it does not come apart when you turn like the original. I accidentally ordered an extra in the Formaggio kickstarter.
[imageid=9214498]

[b]Version:[/b] 1.5 [b]Language:[/b] English [b]Condition:[/b] New, cards are in shrink. Models ready to build. [b]Price:[/b] $950 (And you don't have to pay for shipping)
Contains the following expansions: Expansion of Death Vol. 1 (all of the expansions: 12/13 in all, Dragon King, Dung Beetle Knight, Lion Knight, Role Survivors, Flower Knight, Manhunter, Gorm, Slenderman, Sunstalker, Lonely Tree, Spidicules, Green Knight, and Lion God) AND the Gambler's Chest (Huge expansion, many variants, lots of miniatures) AND the Campaigns of Death Expansion (new rules, new campaigns) - when it ships.
This is an incredible price because I don't want to have to ship it. And you don't want to have to pay for shipping. The base game is in new condition. Everything is still in shrink other than the main box. The other expansions are still in their original shipping boxes.
So why am I selling? Because I just cannot dedicate the table space and time. It looks great, but it is difficult. I have not painted anything and most models are ready to be assembled.
This price is lower than any I could find for this set.
item.comment:
It's not often I can say $950 is a great price, but here we are. Pretty sure this is cheaper than buying on Black Friday (KDM's annual huge sale).
That said, I have everything but Slenderman and (obviously) the unreleased Campaigns of Death. If somebody doesn't take you up on this, I'd be interested in your new Slenderman if you're willing to piece it out (and Campaigns of Death once you have it, which I could likely pick up locally).
Thanks for the offer. I will need to sell these together to keep top value. But much appreciated.

Also includes the following: [thing=2587][/thing] [thing=3609][/thing] [thing=5293][/thing]
All 4 of these are in fantastic condition considering their age. The boxes are definitely worn. But the components are great! Most of the counters are still waiting to be punched. All of the maps and score-sheets are in place. The scenarios are still glued into their original packages. You even get circa-1978 dice in a few cases.
This is for any gamers who want to experience the board game that influenced so many modern war games. The final expansion even includes the basis for "Advanced Squad Leader" before it became a notebook of rules. You will be getting a bit more of a game with this package and less of a rules system.

mechanisms: deck construction, events
In Fate of Witches, the Grand High Witch is dead—and the council is in chaos. As one of the contenders for the title, you’ll need to build the most powerful coven before suspicion, betrayal, or the Witch Hunter’s torch consumes you. This 1–4 player coven-building card game mixes accessible drafting and engine-building with layered strategy and gorgeous, atmospheric art that evokes Darkest Dungeon meets Hellboy. Over rounds divided into Dawn, Day, and Night phases, you’ll recruit witches and familiars, craft potions, wield relics, and unleash spell combos while sabotaging rival covens and bracing for unpredictable event cards. Easy to learn yet full of tactical depth, Fate of Witches shines with replayability and tension—every choice feels like a deal with the dark arts. Whether solo or with friends, it’s a bewitching blend of charm, strategy, and risk that will leave you plotting your next play long after the candles burn out.

Forest Floor is a fast, interactive card game where you’ll grow your garden—and sabotage your rivals! 🌿 Easy to learn but full of clever twists, players race to collect sets of plants while using the unique Mulching mechanic to disrupt others and turn the tide in their favor. With every card you play, timing and prediction are everything—help yourself or hinder someone else? Featuring gorgeous botanical art by Vitalii Vill and a quick 20-minute playtime, Forest Floor is the perfect mix of beauty, strategy, and playful chaos. Grow smart, mulch faster, and claim victory on the forest floor—where only the sharpest gardener survives!

Set sail for adventure in Catan: Explorers & Pirates, the fourth major expansion for The Settlers of Catan. This expansion transforms the familiar island-building classic into a sweeping voyage across uncharted seas. Players explore new islands, trade gold, fend off pirates, and deliver fish and spices to the people of Catan — all across five rich scenarios that blend exploration, resource management, and adventure. Gone are cities and knights; instead, you’ll build ships and port settlements, uncover hidden territories, and earn gold when fortune fails to favor your dice. Each scenario layers new mechanics and missions — from discovering new lands and battling pirate lairs to fishing deep waters and forging alliances with spice islanders. Whether you’re charting new seas in Land Ho! or mastering all three missions in the epic Explorers & Pirates, this expansion turns Catan into a full-blown maritime expedition that rewards curiosity, strategy, and courage on the open waves.

CATAN: Dawn of Humankind ‐ English edition (2022) condition: very good
mechanisms: dice rolling, hexagon grid, random production, resource to move, trading
Catan: Dawn of Humankind reimagines the classic Catan experience as a fast-flowing prehistoric migration game—standalone, lighter, friendlier, and beautifully thematic. Players begin in Africa, guiding early humans as they spread across continents, hunt animals, and develop technologies in a race to 10 points. The core dice-and-trade system remains, but with smoother pacing: simplified costs, no roads or cities, no blocking, and a forgiving 3:1 trade rate mean turns stay active and accessible. Gorgeous components, clever touches like Africa’s drying resources, and a sense of discovery make it an inviting experience for families and casual players alike. It’s less cutthroat and strategic than base Catan, with reduced replayability, but its charm, approachability, and visual appeal make it an excellent entry point for newcomers or a refreshing change of pace for long-time fans.

The Manhattan Project: Energy Empire (2016) base game condition: LIKE NEW
plus EXPANSION CONTENT: --The Manhattan Project: Energy Empire – Cold War (English edition) - VERY RARE (there are 3 BGG listings at $50 $125 $150) condition: like new but without box - The Manhattan Project: Energy Empire – Mexico (2017) promo card - The Manhattan Project: Energy Empire – Missile Crisis (2016) promo card
mechanisms: contracts, dice rolling, die icon resolution, end game bonuses, events, multi-use cards, drafting, income, market, tags, track movement, variable player powers, worker placement, different work types, solo
The Manhattan Project: Energy Empire is a standalone worker-placement and engine-building game where you lead a nation rebuilding after WWII, expanding industry, commerce, and government while managing pollution and global impacts. Instead of warfare, the challenge is balancing economic growth with environmental sustainability. You’ll generate and spend energy dice representing nuclear, solar, and fossil fuels to power actions, build structures, and chain combos across your tableau. With clever mechanics that let players share spaces by paying extra energy, variable nations and achievements, and stunning components like oil barrels and I-beams, Energy Empire delivers a deeply thematic, strategic Euro experience about power, progress, and the price of industrialization. Note: the 2025 version has changed some of the game mechanisms.
The Manhattan Project: Energy Empire – Cold War (2019) is the original modular expansion for the 2016 Energy Empire, adding fresh layers of strategy, player interaction, and variability while preserving the classic ruleset and feel of the first edition. Cold War introduces plug-and-play modules—from espionage actions and megastructures to the doomsday clock, new nations, headlines, and expanded card sets—letting you customize the game’s complexity and pace as you like. These additions open up new scoring routes, create bigger and more competitive action rounds, and offer richer engine-building without changing what fans loved about the base game. It also includes the Clash of Nations solo mode, giving solo players a meaningful challenge built for the original system. Perfect for players who prefer the pre-2025 mechanisms 2019 expansion adds depth, tension, and replayability to the classic Energy Empire experience.
[B]BIN:[/B] $60 includes: base + expansion + 2 promo cards

item.objectname: HERD: The Dinosaur Survival Card Game
item.body:
HERD: The Dinosaur Survival Card Game ‐ English edition (2025) everything new NIS
KICKSTARTER HERD: The Dinosaur Survival Card Game ‐ English edition (2025) HERD DELUXE VERSION pledge bundled with: --Herd Epoch Environments expansion (w/ 5 new playable herds and 2 new card types) --24x14 neoprene playmat --HERD promo card pack: A 15 card promo pack (containing alternate art HERD cards, unique Prey Cards, unique Predator Cards, and a unique HERD.)
mechanisms: card play conflict resolution, roles with asymmetric information, semi-cooperative, turn order
HERD is a beautifully illustrated, semi-cooperative dinosaur survival card game where each player leads a unique herbivore herd—Triceratops, Stegosaurus, Parasaurolophus, Ankylosaurus, or Brontosaurus—through five escalating rounds of Mesozoic danger. Each turn, new predators stalk the Hunting Ground and players must defend their herd using tactical Prey cards, clever timing, and shared survival instincts. The tension ramps up as the Countdown Clock ticks toward zero, forcing players to decide when to sacrifice smaller creatures, when to help another herd, and when to gamble on tough defenses. With its dramatic silhouettes, tarot-sized cards, and a satisfyingly oppressive “predators-everywhere” atmosphere, HERD delivers a rare blend of dinosaur theme, survival pressure, and light cooperation that feels fresh—especially for herbivore fans. Add in the Epoch Environments expansion for migration, hazards, and five more herds, and HERD becomes a thematic, cinematic struggle for group survival that dinosaur lovers won’t want to miss.
[B]BIN:[/B] $80 I don't believe the playmat or promo pack are available in retail preorder. I paid $100 for this set w/ shipping.
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine. 5% discount on purchases of 3+ games, or 10% discount on 6+ games.

Watercolor ‐ English edition (2025) condition: new - NIS by designer Michael Scott (who also made Threehorn)
mechanisms: hand management, ladder climbing, melding and splaying
Watercolor is a clever, calming 2-player race to empty your hand by building progressively higher “numbers” made from same-color or same-value cards—arranged in any order you choose. Sequencing is everything: every time you play a new number, you must pick up a previously played digit, so timing your combos becomes a fun little puzzle. The game adds great variety with Skill Cards inspired by Battle Line tactics, an extra suit, more cards in hand, and multiple ways the table can clear—making it feel wonderfully tuned for two. It’s light, strategic, and perfect for a relaxed coffee break or an easygoing game night. If you enjoy smart dueling card games with a touch of flexibility and creativity, Watercolor is a lovely addition to your collection.
[B]BIN:[/B] $35
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine. 5% discount on purchases of 3+ games, or 10% discount on 6+ games.

ThreeHorn ‐ English edition (2025) condition: new - NIS by designer Michael Scott (who made Watercolor)
mechanisms: card game, set collection, player elimination
ThreeHorn is a light, jazzy, social card game where players draw and discard to build the highest-value same-suit trio before someone calls Showtime. Lowest hand loses a Record token, and once you’re out of tokens, you’re out of the jazz scene! It’s quick to teach, easy to laugh over, and shines most with groups who enjoy the table banter as much as the gameplay. Venue cards add great variety—forcing trades, forming fragile alliances, and shaking up each round with hilarious twists. Inspired by a classic family favorite but snazzed up with modern touches, ThreeHorn plays in minutes and works beautifully with 3–5 players. If you enjoy fast, social card games with personality, this one’s a great fit for your group.

item.body:
Carthago ‐ English-only edition (2018) condition: like new
BUNDLED WITH: Carthago: Merchants & Guilds – Golden Achievements (2018) Carthago: Merchants & Guilds – Support of the Guilds (2018)
designers Ralph Bienert, Bernd Eisenstein (who made Pirates of Maracaibo, Peloponnes, Discordia, Alea Iacta Est, Order of the Guilded Compass, Papyria)
mechanisms: action points, deck building, hand management, pickup and deliver, set collection, trading, worker placement
Carthago: Merchants & Guilds is a wonderfully tense, card-driven euro where every decision counts as you claw your way to power in ancient Carthage. With multi-use cards, tight hand management, and a smart action-wheel system, players juggle loading ships, financing risky naval expeditions, and fighting for precious seats in the Merchant’s Guild—all while racing opponents for ships that slide through the harbor and constantly reshape your plans. It’s quick, brutal, and rewarding, delivering meaty choices in a compact package with beautiful artwork and language-independent components. If you love tactical efficiency puzzles like Concordia or Heaven & Ale and enjoy that delicious “so many good options, not enough actions” feeling, Carthago offers a punchy, strategic experience that shines once you settle into its rhythm—perfect for gamers who want depth without a long rules overhead.
[B]BIN:[/B] $15 w/ 2 expansions
I will be at the VFM TABLE G3 and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine. 5% discount on purchases of 3+ games, or 10% discount on 6+ games.

Letter Jam ‐ English edition (2019) condition: Like New
BUNDLED WITH: Letter Jam: Bonus Chip #9 (2019) Additional chip for Letter Jam, allowing 9-letter words.
mechanisms: deduction, party game, word game, communication limits, cooperative game
Letter Jam is a fantastic cooperative word-deduction game for 2–6 players—easy to bring to game nights, simple to teach after one round, and endlessly satisfying once the table starts firing on all cylinders. Each player has a hidden letter they can’t see, and everyone works together to build clever clue-words from the visible letters around the table, using numbered tokens to spell out hints that help others decode their own letters. It’s accessible like a family game, social like a light party game, but structured and thoughtful enough for dedicated word-gamers. With sturdy components, big colorful tokens, and that addictive “Aha, now I know my letter!” moment, Letter Jam shines with groups who love puzzles, teamwork, and creative wordplay—and it’s one of those rare games that newcomers understand after a single round, yet experienced players can challenge themselves with deeper, more elegant clues. A must-have for clubs, families, and anyone who enjoys cooperative deduction with a fun, lightly party-game vibe.
[B]BIN:[/B] $15
I will be at the VFM TABLE G3 and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine. 5% discount on purchases of 3+ games, or 10% discount on 6+ games.

item.body:
The Scarlet Pimpernel (Regular edition) condition: Like New
mechanisms: area majority/influence, area movement, contracts, network and route building, variable player powers, worker placement, spies/secret agents
The Scarlet Pimpernel is a gorgeous semi-cooperative strategy game where players join the League to help the legendary masked hero rescue innocents during the French Revolution—and compete to become his most trusted advisor. Across seven missions, you’ll race around an 18th-century map of England and France placing cubes to secure routes, gather disguises, horses, forged papers, political allies, and complete key objectives before the mission triggers. Everyone wants the Pimpernel to succeed… but only your cubes score if you time your placements well, hold area majorities, grab the right Special Favor powers, and manipulate when each mission ends. With stunning Ian O’Toole artwork, thick, deluxe components, and a clever blend of shared goals and cutthroat timing, The Scarlet Pimpernel delivers a fresh, highly interactive euro experience that feels thematic, tactical, and wonderfully tense—perfect for players who enjoy sneaky semi-coop decisions wrapped in a beautifully produced historical adventure.

item.body:
Ekö (Multilingual first edition) 2015 condition: Like New
mechanisms: grid movement, abstract strategy, modular board
Ekö is a gorgeous, deterministic abstract strategy game where stacked wooden discs become armies, surprise attacks, and the foundation for buildings that score you points or shift area control. After a randomized setup, every move is pure tactics—sliding stacks across the board, striking weaker foes (or daring kamikaze hits), reinforcing dwindling forces, or sacrificing pieces to construct villages, towers, and castles. With two win conditions—eliminate your opponents or reach 12 VP—Ekö creates a tense, elegant puzzle full of unexpected twists: even a single piece can topple a mighty stack of four, the emperor breaks ties and becomes a high-value target, and buildings double as both scoring tools and reinforcement blockers. It plays brilliantly at 2 players and cleverly with 3–4, offering a deep, beautiful, and totally overlooked abstract that rewards bold plays and razor-sharp decision-making. If you enjoy accessible rules with rich strategic depth, Ekö is one of those rare hidden gems that only gets better the more you explore it.
[B]BIN:[/B] $20

mechanisms: area movement, auction/bidding, dice rolling, hand management, player elimination, point to point movement, set collection, trading, wargame, negotiation, economic, political
Attack! Deluxe adds to the base game by setting the stage for combat on the Pacific Front. It introduces bold new mechanisms with expanded Naval Combat, player government styles, new technology research, and seasonal combat. As the leader of a world power, you can choose to control trade routes on all seven seas or you can blitz the sovereign shores of your nearest nations by land: build the biggest army and crush your enemies before they crush you, or choke the life out of them by cutting their economic supply. All is fair in love and war after all!
This is the upgraded huge expansion to Attack! with "350 miniatures" (they are tiny). The cards in Attack! Deluxe replace all of the Attack! base game cards to ensure uniformity, with these cards having better quality base card stock and linen finish with playing card varnish.

Stamp Swap ‐ English edition (2024) condition: New - NIS
designer Paul Salomon (who made Honey Buzz, Genotype, Periodic, Virulence, Corgi Pileup)
mechanisms: Drafting, I Cut You Choose, Tile Placement
BIN $25
Stamp Swap turns the surprisingly cozy world of stamp collecting into a clever, interactive strategy game where bluffing, set collection, and smart timing matter just as much as the adorable artwork. Designed by Paul Salomon (Honey Buzz, Genotype) and published by Stonemaier Games, this 1–5 player title blends an “I split, you choose” drafting twist with polyomino-style album placement and evolving scoring goals across three fast, engaging rounds. Players draft stamps from a shared pool, divide them into tempting (or deceptive!) piles for opponents, then arrange their growing collections to impress contest judges—while chasing rare gold-foil stamps, specialist bonuses, and finale scoring. At higher player counts the game shines, offering rich interaction, tactical splits, and delicious tension as everyone evaluates colors, themes, sizes, and values at the table. Beautiful components, intuitive rules, and a surprisingly thinky solo mode make Stamp Swap a charming, strategic filler that delights collectors-at-heart—even those who never thought they cared about stamps.
I will be at the VFM and that is the preferred meeting place. Cash, Paypal F&F, Venmo, CashApp are fine. 5% discount on purchases of 3+ games, or 10% discount on 6+ games.
